It's hard to argue with him. Kiffin was ready and willing to take advantage of this ruling because he's looking for any competitive advantage, no matter how ridiculous it might be. It's unfair to the college athletes on the LSU roster, unfair to Clemson and unfair that there's so little meaningful oversight of the sport.

Not that this game needed any more drama and intrigue, but Swinney’s comments illustrate how most opposing coaches and teams will feel about playing LSU this season should those players be allowed to stay with the Tigers. Still, it would be sweet revenge for Clemson if the Tigers were able to pull off the upset anyway.

articles.title: Tyler Robinson to face trial in Charlie Kirk assassination as judge keeps death penalty on table
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Garrett Tenney has the latest on a Utah judge's ruling that accused Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson will stand trial on aggravated murder charges and remain eligible for th...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Garrett Tenney has the latest on a Utah judge's ruling that accused Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson will stand trial on aggravated murder charges and remain eligible for the death penalty, after prosecutors argued he knowingly endangered others during the 2025 shooting at a Turning Point USA event, on 'Jesse Watters Primetime.'

Tyler Robinson, the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk, will stand trial after a Utah judge ruled Tuesday that prosecutors presented enough evidence to move forward on all seven charges against him.

Robinson pleaded not guilty to all charges moments after Judge Tony Graf issued the ruling. Graf also ruled that prosecutors may continue seeking the death penalty in the case. He found that the state established probable cause for the victim-targeting allegation, allowing the capital sentencing enhancement to move forward.

"Viewed in the light most favorable to the prosecution, this evidence is sufficient at this stage to support a reasonable belief that the defendant is the individual who shot and killed Charlie Kirk," Graf said.

TYLER ROBINSON HEARING COULD DECIDE DEATH PENALTY FATE, FINALLY SEE PLEA IN CHARLIE KIRK CASE

Tyler Robinson, charged in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, sits as his defense team argues before the judge during closing arguments at his preliminary hearing in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026. (Francisco Kjolseth | The Salt Lake Tribune)

Graf emphasized that the standard at a preliminary hearing is not whether prosecutors have proven their case beyond a reasonable doubt, but whether there is enough evidence to send the charges to trial.

"Whether the state can prove the aggravating circumstance beyond a reasonable doubt remains for trial," Graf said. "Count one is bound over for trial."

PROSECUTORS HAMMER TYLER ROBINSON'S BID TO DERAIL DEATH PENALTY IN CHARLIE KIRK MURDER CASE

Tyler Robinson pleaded not guilty to all seven charges filed by prosecutors. (Francisco Kjolseth | The Salt Lake Tribune)

The judge also sided with prosecutors on the victim-targeting allegation against Robinson, concluding that the state had established probable cause for the allegation.

Graf ultimately ordered Robinson to stand trial on all seven charges: aggravated murder; felony discharge of a firearm causing serious bodily injury; two counts of obstruction of justice; two counts of witness tampering; and committing a violent offense in the presence of a child.

CHARLIE KIRK MURDER CASE AS 'STRAIGHT-FORWARD' AS IT GETS, PROSECUTORS ARGUE AS CASE NEARS TRIAL DECISION

(Francisco Kjolseth | The Salt Lake Tribune) Tyler Robinson, charged in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, sits during closing arguments at his preliminary hearing in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026. ( )

The aggravated murder and firearm charges are first-degree felonies, while the obstruction charges are second-degree felonies and the witness tampering charges are third-degree felonies. The final charge,committing a violent offense in the presence of a child, is a Class A misdemeanor.

The court moved directly into Robinson’s arraignment after Graf issued his ruling. The defense waived a formal reading of the charges, and Robinson’s attorney entered not guilty pleas on his behalf.

The ruling came hours after another courtroom fight over whether cameras should be allowed to remain in the high-profile proceedings.

Following closed-door arguments Tuesday morning and additional arguments in open court, Graf again denied a defense motion seeking to remove cameras from the courtroom.

Robinson’s attorneys had raised concerns about the intense publicity surrounding the case, including what they described as online marketplace gambling tied to its outcome.

ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON DEALT COURTROOM BLOW, DAYS BEFORE PIVOTAL HEARING

Graf ruled cameras could remain, subject to the restrictions laid out in his courtroom decorum order.

Kirk, 31, was shot and killed Sept. 10, 2025, while speaking before thousands at an outdoor Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah. Prosecutors have accused Robinson of firing the fatal shot from an elevated position overlooking the crowd.

ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON FIGHTS BACK AS PROSECUTORS' SPRAWLING CASE COMES INTO FOCUS

Erika Kirk departs court in Provo, Utah, Monday, July 6, 2026. The widow of Charlie Kirk was attending the first day of preliminary hearings against, Tyler Robinson who is on trial for Kirk's murder. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)

Before Tuesday’s hearing ended, Jeff Neiman, an attorney representing Kirk’s family, urged the court to move the case toward trial without unnecessary delays and pushed back against comments defense attorney Richard Novak made about Kirk.

"Charlie devoted his life to building a community of over a million young people rooted in faith and freedom. He had hard conversations others were too afraid to have," Neiman told the court.

ERIKA KIRK COMFORTS A STRANGER IN TEARS DURING HEARING FOR HUSBAND'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON

Charlie Kirk throws hats to the crowd after arriving at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah, on Sept. 10, 2025. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

"Charlie was the opposite of hate," he continued. "Firing a bullet into a crowd and assassinating him. That is hate."

Neiman said Kirk’s family recognizes Robinson’s right to a fair trial but wants the case to move forward swiftly.

UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE

"The United States Constitution guarantees criminal defendants many rights. The right to delay is not among them," Neiman said. "The defendant is entitled to a fair trial, and he must be given one. But nothing more is owed."

"We have no doubt this court will give the defendant a fair trial," he added. "We ask that it do so swiftly."

Neiman later specifically asked Graf to set a trial date at Robinson’s next court appearance so Kirk’s family would know when the case is expected to move forward.

Robinson is due back in court Oct. 23 at 1 p.m. local time for a status conference and has been ordered to appear. A trial date could be set at that hearing.

Following Tuesday's hearing, Kirk's family said Graf's decision to send Robinson to trial marks "an important step" in their pursuit of justice nearly one year after Kirk's death.

"Today's decision, which comes nearly a year since Charlie was taken from us, marks an important step in our family's pursuit of justice for him," the family said in a statement.

The family said every stage of the case has carried "the weight of all that Charlie's murder has taken," especially for Kirk's children, who "will grow up without their father."

As the case moves toward trial, the family said they remain committed to seeking justice for Charlie while praying for "a transparent and timely process."

Fox News' Lee Ross contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Ohio man accused of vandalizing JD Vance’s home pleads guilty
articles.excerpt:
A North Dakota man has been charged with felony criminal mischief after police say he keyed a Tesla Cybertruck in West Fargo. (Mitch Benson via Storyful)

An Ohio man accused of vandalizing Vice Presi...
articles.body_text:
A North Dakota man has been charged with felony criminal mischief after police say he keyed a Tesla Cybertruck in West Fargo. (Mitch Benson via Storyful)

An Ohio man accused of vandalizing Vice President JD Vance’s Cincinnati home earlier this year pleaded guilty in federal court Tuesday, officials said.

William D. DeFoor, 26, reportedly caused tens of thousands of dollars in damage Jan. 5 when he used a hammer to smash multiple windows at Vance’s unoccupied home.

DeFoor specifically admitted to acts of physical violence against government officials or property, as well as the willful injury or depredation of U.S. government property, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Ohio.

His defense attorney previously said the assaults were not politically motivated and that DeFoor suffers from mental health issues. Court records show DeFoor has a history of criminal cases involving findings of mental incompetency.

SUSPECT IN VANCE HOME VANDALISM HAS HAD MULTIPLE RUN-INS WITH THE LAW, DEMANDED TO BE CALLED JULIA

William D. DeFoor remained jailed for nearly nine months after allegedly vandalizing Vice President JD Vance’s Cincinnati home. (WXIX; Hamilton County Sheriff's Office)

"Perpetrators like DeFoor, who put that freedom at risk, particularly through violent, destructive actions, will, like here, be vigorously prosecuted," U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II said in a statement Tuesday.

According to court documents, DeFoor was detained around midnight after Secret Service agents observed him near the front fence of Vance’s protected residence. Vance and his family were in Washington, D.C., at the time of the incident.

SECRET SERVICE AGENT ON JD VANCE'S DETAIL INVESTIGATED FOR ALLEGEDLY LEAKING OPERATIONAL SECURITY INFO

While wielding a hammer, DeFoor reportedly breached the property line at the driveway and proceeded to target an unmarked federal law enforcement vehicle blocking the driveway entrance. DeFoor used the weapon to strike the driver’s-side window three times, prosecutors said.

As Secret Service agents responded to the scene, DeFoor ignored all commands to stop and drop the weapon, according to charging documents.

He then used the hammer to break large, historic glass windows across the front of the home, officials said.

The attack reportedly damaged components of an enhanced security system located on each window. The equipment was owned by the U.S. government and valued at more than $28,000, prosecutors said.

ATTORNEY FOR SUSPECT IN VANCE HOME VANDALISM RULES OUT POSSIBLE MOTIVATION

William DeFoor, 26, appears in court on Tuesday, Jan. 6, 2026, for non-federal charges in connection with the vandalism of Vice President JD Vance's Cincinnati home. (WXIX)

Secret Service agents and Cincinnati police officers eventually detained DeFoor after he tried to flee on foot.

Gerace on Tuesday further condemned the violence, saying assaults against U.S. officials will be prosecuted.

"Acts of violence directed against our political leaders, their families, or property, have no place in our society and will not be tolerated. Our elected leaders, at all levels of government, must be permitted to carry out their duties free from threats, vandalism, and other forms of violence," Gerace said.

According to court records, DeFoor has a history of mental health issues in Hamilton County spanning more than two years.

FBI sources previously told Fox News that when DeFoor was arrested, he demanded to be called "Julia."

In April 2023, DeFoor was charged with trespassing at University of Cincinnati Health Psychiatric Emergency Services after police said he refused to leave the premises. He was ruled incompetent to stand trial, and the case was later dismissed.

The following year, DeFoor was charged with two counts of vandalism after windows at a Hyde Park business were broken. The case was referred to a mental health docket, with treatment ordered in lieu of conviction.

Vice President JD Vance and his family were in Washington, D.C., when the vandalism incident happened at his Cincinnati residence. (Bonnie Cash/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Hamilton County Court later approved an application granting DeFoor’s mother legal guardianship after finding him incompetent by reason of mental illness.

Fox News Digital’s Stephen Sorace and Greg Wehner contributed to this report.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: What to know about Germany’s drone attack accusations against Russia
articles.excerpt:
Germany has formally accused Russia of attempting an attack last month at the Leipzig-Halle airport, a state-owned facility in the eastern part of the country.

On Tuesday, German Interior Minister Al...
articles.body_text:
Germany has formally accused Russia of attempting an attack last month at the Leipzig-Halle airport, a state-owned facility in the eastern part of the country.

On Tuesday, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said his country’s intelligence community had determined that a drone discovered at the airport was consistent with Russian technology. The drone had been bearing explosives, according to official reports.

The announcement triggered several retaliatory measures, including the announcement that Germany would shut down a Russian consulate.

The incident is seen as part of a growing trend in Europe, where officials fear Russia is mounting a campaign of intimidation against members of the NATO military alliance.

What was found at the Leipzig airport? How have officials responded? And what does it say about tensions between Europe and Russia as Moscow’s war in Ukraine drags on? Read on for a quick explainer on the basics.

An explosive-laden drone was found near a cargo plane belonging to the Ukrainian firm Antonov Airlines on the evening of August 4.

An employee flagged the drone, which was located in a cargo area near a runway, resulting in a temporary shutdown at the Leipzig-Halle airport, a major cargo hub in the eastern German state of Saxony.

Specialists were called in to defuse the explosives with a robot. A second drone was reportedly destroyed after it collided with an aeroplane near the airport.

Dobrindt, Germany’s interior minister, said investigators identified a configuration and components resembling those seen in Russia’s war against Ukraine.

“Taken together, the police investigations, the pattern and intelligence findings prove a Russian responsibility for the attempted attack at Leipzig airport,” Dobrindt said.

Germany’s government has not publicly shared specifics connecting the incident to Moscow or released all the evidence.

But Dobrindt said the device reflected “a high degree of technical expertise”. He added, however, that the task of carrying out the attack appears to have fallen to “low-level agents”, whom he described as people acting “on behalf of Russian state entities”. He did not specify which ones.

Germany has taken a series of retaliatory actions since announcing the intelligence community’s findings.

Starting on September 18, a Russian consulate in Bonn, a major German city on the Rhine River, will be shuttered. The Russian House, a cultural gathering place in Berlin, will also be closed, though the date has yet to be determined.

German leaders said they would also recommend more Russians be added to the European Union’s sanctions list and consider heightening entry controls for Russian citizens.

The German Foreign Ministry has also summoned Russia’s ambassador to the country to discuss the incident.

Moscow has denied it had anything to do with the drone. The Russian Embassy in Berlin called the claims absurd and warned that the accusations would have consequences.

Separately, Russian President Vladimir Putin accused the government of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of pointing the finger at Moscow to distract from domestic problems and falling approval ratings.

He also suggested that Germany had planted evidence to frame Russia for the drone incident.

NATO allies like Poland, Italy, the United Kingdom, Sweden and the Czech Republic have all backed Berlin’s claims against Moscow.

“Whenever Russian hybrid activities target one of our allies, we are all exposed,” the Czech Foreign Ministry posted on social media.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she would discuss the incident with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, and EU foreign ministers are expected to prepare a joint response.

Since February 2022, Ukraine has been battling a war that began with Russia’s full-scale invasion of its neighbour.

There has been speculation that Moscow’s increasing military threats in Europe are designed to weaken NATO support for Kyiv.

Ukraine has welcomed Germany’s measures against Russia, with Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksii Makeiev praising Berlin’s response on Tuesday.

Germany has been a key strategic partner for Ukraine, and in April, the two countries unveiled a security cooperation agreement that would strengthen joint air defences.

As part of the deal, Berlin agreed to fund missile contracts for Kyiv, and the two would collaborate on drone co-production.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that his country’s airspace is becoming increasingly unsafe for civilian aviation, with both sides in the war increasingly relying on drone warfare.

Critics have long warned that Russia is taking an increasingly aggressive stance towards Europe, which has opposed its invasion of Ukraine.

The Associated Press news agency has logged some 200 incidents of sabotage and malign activity in Europe since the 2022 invasion.

Those acts include cyberattacks, espionage, disinformation campaigns, arson and interference with infrastructure.

One case, in March 2024, involved a warehouse in east London being set on fire. The facility stored aid for Ukraine, and prosecutors blamed the attack on members of the Russian-backed Wagner Group, a paramilitary organisation.

Such low-level operations are often called “hybrid” attacks, as they remain below the threshold of open conflict but still succeed in sowing unease through violence.

Germany says covert operations like the attempted drone attack at the Leipzig airport are meant to undermine the country’s political backing for Ukraine in its defence against Russia.

The war has stretched for more than four years, and Ukrainian officials have warned that the coming winter may prove the most challenging yet.

The attempted drone attack also comes at a pivotal time for German politics.

On September 6, the eastern province of Saxony-Anhalt is holding elections, and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is hoping to make gains, building in part on public weariness with the war.

The AfD has called for strengthening ties with Russia and has been critical of support for Ukraine. It is currently leading in public opinion polls ahead of the vote.

articles.title: Top Democrat survives double-barreled challenge as party’s Israel divide hits home
articles.excerpt:
Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., weighs in on the Democratic Party’s internal debate over U.S. aid to Israel and more during ‘The Sunday Briefing.’

House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark toppled two progress...
articles.body_text:
Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., weighs in on the Democratic Party’s internal debate over U.S. aid to Israel and more during ‘The Sunday Briefing.’

House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark toppled two progressive challengers Tuesday in Massachusetts' safely Democratic 5th Congressional District, surviving a primary fight that put Gaza and pro-Israel political spending at the center of the race.

Clark, who won handily Tuesday night against fellow Democratic Party contenders Jonathan Paz and Tarik Samman, was first elected in 2013 during a special election and has held her position as House Democratic Whip since 2022.

The second-highest ranking Democrat after House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, Clark has helped lead opposition to Republican spending, immigration and health-care measures, including recent messaging against ICE funding and GOP cuts to Head Start and Medicaid.

MEET THE FAR-LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT IN 2026 MIDTERMS

WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 30: U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark (D-MA) arrives for a leadership election meeting with the Democratic caucus in the Longworth House Office Building on Capitol Hill November 30, 2022 in Washington, DC. Clark is running for the number two position in House Democratic leadership following the departure of Rep. Steny Hoyer (D-MD) from the leadership group. (Photo by Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

She ran against former city councilor, educator and union organizer Paz and 27-year-old Harvard Law School researcher and union organizer Samman.

Clark fended off two left-wing challengers who sought to make Gaza and pro-Israel political money central issues in the safely blue Boston-area primary.

Her fundraising operation dwarfed both challengers, raising $4.5 million, while Paz raised $88,500 and Samman $43,800, according to FEC filings.

PELOSI-BACKED DEMOCRAT LOSES AFTER $10M FLOOD OF CRYPTO, PRO-ISRAEL MONEY

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., right, joined at center-left by Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., the House minority whip, rallies Democrats against the Republican budget plan, on the House steps at the Capitol in Washington on Tuesday, Feb. 25. (AP/J. Scott Applewhite)

While AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, endorsed Clark and has contributed to her campaign in the past, she has taken a critical stance toward the Israeli government’s handling of the war in Gaza.

AIPAC is an influential pro-Israel lobbying group that has been criticized for advocating for U.S. military aid to Israel amid the war in Gaza.

Last year, she used the word "genocide" at a district event before clarifying that she was not accusing Israel of genocide; then in July, she voted to cut $3.3 billion in U.S. military aid, saying Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government had failed to meet U.S. interests and values.

Clark has continued to support Israel as a sovereign Jewish state and backed U.S. assistance for some Israeli defensive systems but is critical against Netanyahu.

TOP HOUSE DEMOCRAT SAYS ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVISTS’ THREATS KEPT HIM FROM TOWN HALLS FOR A YEAR

FILE - U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., speaks during a news conference on protecting women's reproductive health care, Thursday, July 28, 2022, on Capitol Hill in Washington. An adult child of Clark's was arrested during a protest late Saturday, Jan. 21, 2023, on Boston Common and later charged with assault after a police officer was injured. ((AP Photo/Mariam Zuhaib, File))

Samman and Paz have argued that while Clark has increasingly criticized Israel’s conduct in Gaza, she has yet to renounce the AIPAC money she has accepted.

Clark ran unopposed in 2024. Her most recent general-election opponent was Republican Caroline Colarusso, whom Clark defeated 74% to 26% in 2022.

Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Iran says US bombed a wedding party in Sirik, killing five
articles.excerpt:
Iran has accused the United States of bombing a house during a wedding celebration in the southern county of Sirik, killing at least five people, including a child.

Esmaeil Baghaei, the spokesman for...
articles.body_text:
Iran has accused the United States of bombing a house during a wedding celebration in the southern county of Sirik, killing at least five people, including a child.

Esmaeil Baghaei, the spokesman for Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said the “brutal” attack hit a residence in the city of Kuhestak early on Wednesday.

The state-owned Press TV reported that at least five people were killed.

Reza Shahidiyan, the governor of Sirik county, later told the IRIB state broadcaster that 63 others were wounded, and that 50 of the victims were women and children. All of the wounded have been taken to a hospital in the nearby city of Minab and were “in stable condition,” he said.

The semi-official Fars news agency meanwhile published an account from a child who survived the blast.

The child said he heard fighter jets before he arrived at the venue.

“When we arrived there, an explosion occurred. It was very intense. Bricks, stones, and cement hit me in the face and head, and many others were injured,” he said. “Everyone was just ordinary civilians.”

The reports came as the US military announced a new wave of strikes against “Iranian military targets”, saying it followed attempted attacks by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US military said it had hit Iranian air defence sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites.

The strikes follow a weekend exchange of fire and come amid a continuing standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blockaded since the start of the US and Israel’s war on the country on February 28

Baghaei, the Iranian spokesman, promised to respond to the US’s latest attacks.

“This cruelty cannot be separated from the chain of atrocities that preceded in it,” he said, pointing to attacks on the city of Minab and Lamerd on the first day of the war. In Minab, US forces struck an elementary school, killed more than 150 people, and in Lamerd, they hit a sport hall, killing at least 21 people.

In addition to Kuhestak, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported further explosions in the south of the country, including in Konarak, Bandar Abbas and on Qeshm Island.

Iran’s military said it retaliated by attacking US bases and assets in Jordan, Bahrain and Iraq. Kuwait also reported intercepting drones.

articles.title: House Democrat survives left-flank challenge as Bernie volunteer mounts insurgent bid
articles.excerpt: Sen.John Fetterman, Democrat from Pennsylvania, asserts that an official anti-Israel stance by the Democratic Party would be his 'red line,' potentially leading him to leave the party. A recent House ...
articles.body_text:
Sen.John Fetterman, Democrat from Pennsylvania, asserts that an official anti-Israel stance by the Democratic Party would be his 'red line,' potentially leading him to leave the party. A recent House vote saw 103 Democrats block aid to Israel, signaling a major shift.

Rep. Jake Auchincloss advanced Tuesday against Jason Poulos in Massachusetts’ 4th Congressional District.

Auchincloss has held his seat since 2021, facing his first Democratic primary challenge since winning the seat.

Progressive challenger Poulos is an AI policy researcher who has been critical of Auchincloss regarding past support for military aid to Israel and ties to AIPAC while calling for an end to U.S. military assistance to Israel.

PROGRESSIVE WAVE CRASHES IN SUN BELT BATTLEGROUND AS MODERATE HOLDS HIS SEAT

Rep. Jake Auchincloss, D-Mass., speaks during the House Democrats' news conference on the Republican economic agenda in the Capitol on Wednsday, April 9, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Poulos, who previously volunteered for Bernie Sanders’ campaign, ran on Medicare-for-all, universal basic income, taxes on corporate automation, stronger unions, student-debt cancellation. He also wanted to reduce military spending and end U.S. military aid to Israel.

While Auchincloss is endorsed by AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, he been critical of aspects of Israel's conduct in Gaza by saying some Israeli actions in 2025 "crossed lines" on humanitarian conditions.

AIPAC is an pro-Israel influential lobbying group that has been criticized for advocating for U.S. military aid to Israel amid the war in Gaza.

HOUSE DEMOCRATS FRACTURE BADLY OVER MASSIE AMENDMENT TO CUT $3.3B IN U.S. AID TO ISRAEL

President Donald Trump hosts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago on Dec. 29, 2025, with talks addressing Iran’s renewed threats and potential progress on the next phase of the Gaza peace framework. (Israel Government Press Office)

In July, Auchincloss voted with more than 100 House Democrats to eliminate $3.3 billion in U.S. military financing for Israel, while maintaining his support for the U.S.-Israel alliance.

Auchincloss campaigned on lowering housing and healthcare costs, promoting economic growth and positioning Democrats to better confront the economic disruption caused by AI.

UNITED STATES - OCTOBER 22: Aerial view of the Pentagon building in Arlington, Va., on Wednesday, October 22, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Auchincloss, who succeeded Joe Kennedy III, comes from a prominent Boston medical family.

He had previously been a registered Republican and worked on then-Gov. Charlie Baker’s campaign, a line his primary opponents used against him. He later returned to the Democratic Party.

Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Trump taps ‘true warrior’ Hung Cao as Navy secretary after 4 months as acting leader
articles.excerpt:
Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao discusses U.S. military assets in the Middle East and Iran's strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’

President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that...
articles.body_text:
Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao discusses U.S. military assets in the Middle East and Iran's strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’

President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that he is nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to permanently lead the service, calling the former Navy special operations officer a "true WARRIOR" and urging the Senate to quickly confirm him.

Cao has served as acting secretary for the past four months, overseeing the Navy and Marine Corps as the Trump administration pushes to expand U.S. shipbuilding and strengthen the military’s maritime capabilities.

"I am pleased to nominate a true WARRIOR, Hung Cao, to become the next Secretary of the Navy," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"We need Patriots like Hung leading our Navy and Marine Corps, and I can think of no one better than him to make sure our Great Navy and Marine Corps remain the FIERCEST and BEST Force the World has ever seen," the president continued.

TRUMP PRAISES OUSTED NAVY SECRETARY PHELAN AMID TENSIONS WITH PENTAGON LEADERSHIP

Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao testifies during the Senate Armed Services Committee hearing titled "The Posture of the Department of the Navy in review of the Defense Authorization Request for FY2027 and the Future Years Defense Program," in the Dirksen building on Tuesday, May 19, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Trump called on the Senate to move quickly on the nomination, pointing to Cao’s tenure already leading the department.

SENATE REPUBLICANS CONFIRM NEARLY 50 OF TRUMP'S PICKS FOR ENERGY, LAND MANAGEMENT

"The Senate needs to confirm this Warfighter, ASAP, so he can continue the fantastic work he has been doing over the past 4 months," Trump wrote.

Cao thanked Trump shortly after the announcement and said his priorities would continue to include shipbuilding and homeland defense.

AS CHINA TENSIONS LOOM, US TEMPORARILY PAUSES TAIWAN WEAPONS SALES DUE TO IRAN WAR, ACTING NAVY SECRETARY SAYS

President Trump praised Hung Cao as a "true WARRIOR" and urged the Senate to quickly confirm him as Navy secretary, saying Cao is the best person to lead the Navy and Marine Corps and strengthen shipbuilding and homeland defense. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"Thank you, Mr. President. It’s an honor of a lifetime to lead the great warriors of the Navy and Marine Corps team," Cao wrote on X. "I’m grateful for your leadership and support as we continue to get after shipbuilding and ensure the defense of the homeland."

Cao is a retired Navy captain who served for 25 years in uniform after graduating from the U.S. Naval Academy. His military career included service in special operations and deployments to combat zones, including Iraq and Afghanistan.

The Virginia Republican later entered politics, mounting an unsuccessful bid for Congress in 2022 before challenging Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine for his Senate seat in 2024.

Trump endorsed Cao during the 2024 campaign, touting his military background. Cao ultimately lost to Kaine before joining the Trump administration and taking over the Navy in an acting capacity earlier this year.

TRUMP TAPS ACTING LABOR SECRETARY KEITH SONDERLING FOR PERMANENT ROLE PENDING SENATE CONFIRMATION

Under Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao acknowledged the impact of the COVID-19 vaccine mandate on service members dismissed from the military. (U.S. Navy)

If confirmed by the Senate, Cao would formally assume responsibility for the Department of the Navy, which includes both the Navy and Marine Corps.

The White House and the U.S. Navy did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

articles.title: IAEA says Syria built a nuclear reactor in Deir Az Zor under al-Assad
articles.excerpt:
The United Nations nuclear watchdog has confirmed that Syria tried to construct a nuclear reactor in the eastern province of Deir Az Zor under ousted former President Bashar al-Assad.

The Internation...
articles.body_text:
The United Nations nuclear watchdog has confirmed that Syria tried to construct a nuclear reactor in the eastern province of Deir Az Zor under ousted former President Bashar al-Assad.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), in a confidential report seen by news agencies on Tuesday, said it visited several sites in Syria in August and carried out verification work.

Based on observations at the Deir Az Zor site, the agency said it confirms “that the cooling infrastructure which has now been uncovered is consistent with that of a nuclear reactor”. The agency said it would continue to monitor the activities at the site “as the excavation work progresses”.

Syria was believed to have operated an extensive undeclared nuclear programme under al-Assad that included a nuclear reactor built by North Korea in Deir Az Zor.

The site only became public knowledge after Israel launched air strikes in 2007 that destroyed the facility. Syria later levelled the site and never responded fully to the IAEA’s questions about it.

Israel is believed to have its own undeclared atomic weapons programme that makes it the only country in the Middle East with nuclear bombs. Israel neither confirms nor denies having atomic weapons.

Following al-Assad’s removal in early December 2024, the new government agreed to give IAEA inspectors access to suspected former nuclear sites.

The agency took samples at the site in 2024 and reported last year that they contained uranium particles.

In its Tuesday report, the IAEA said it was also able to “establish that the former Syrian authorities had failed to report nuclear material, facilities and activities”.

Besides the nuclear reactor under construction at Deir Az Zor, the IAEA listed a fuel fabrication plant, where the nuclear fuel for the reactor was manufactured, and a location where the nuclear fuel, as well as uranium scrap and waste, were stored.

During the visit to Syria, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi and a team of senior inspectors also visited a previously undeclared site.

The new Syrian administration notified the agency of the site’s existence in a July 17 letter and invited the IAEA “to cooperate with the Syrian authorities in the inspection and verification of the site and of any nuclear material to be potentially found”.

The IAEA said in its report that this new site contained “natural uranium metal in the form of fuel rods with cladding”.

The agency verified the material and confirmed “the presence of around 73 tonnes of natural uranium metal”. The agency reported that “all of this nuclear material is currently subject to Agency containment and surveillance measures”.

The new Syrian authorities have also expressed an interest in developing a civilian nuclear energy programme and said any nuclear material found in the country would remain in Syria’s custody under international safeguards.

articles.title: AOC caught off guard when asked by TMZ whether she'd ever date a conservative after reported split from fiancé
articles.excerpt: Greg Gutfeld reacts to the news that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez split from her longtime fiancé, Riley Roberts. He breaks down the relationship update and jokingly predicts that the progressive cong...
articles.body_text:
Greg Gutfeld reacts to the news that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez split from her longtime fiancé, Riley Roberts. He breaks down the relationship update and jokingly predicts that the progressive congresswoman will end up marrying a police officer next.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., was caught off guard when the progressive lawmaker was asked by TMZ whether she'd date a conservative.

TMZ DC managing editor Charlie Cotton approached Ocasio-Cortez outside Capitol Hill on the heels of her reported split from fiancé Riley Roberts to ask about her dating habits.

"Would you ever date a conservative?" Cotton asked. "Is that [something] you'd ever entertain?"

AOC DOCUMENTS EGG-FREEZING JOURNEY, TAKES AIM AT TRUMP ADMIN OVER WOMEN'S REPRODUCTIVE CHOICES

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., departs following a vote at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. (Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The "Squad" member immediately laughed at the question.

"Um, I'd have to say... probably not," Ocasio-Cortez responded, chuckling again.

CARVILLE TORCHES DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS AS 'PACK OF FOOLS,' PRAISES AOC'S POLITICAL EVOLUTION

When pressed about her reluctance to date across the aisle, Ocasio-Cortez clarified there's "no foul" to those who can put politics aside for love.

"I think a lot of politics sometimes, at least for me, is about values and being aligned in values is tremendously important," Ocasio-Cortez said.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. reportedly split from her fiancé Riley Roberts. (James Devaney/GC Images)

Ocasio-Cortez's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Dating someone with opposing politics was certainly not as taboo in past decades as it is in today's polarized climate. Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville, famously married to former GOP consultant Mary Matalin, spoke with Fox News Digital last year about finding love regardless of political party.

The former Clinton operative lamented how people in the modern era "use politics as a reason to date or not date somebody," something he ultimately disregarded when he was an eligible bachelor.

"In my case, I wasn't good-looking enough. I had to broaden the base, okay," Carville chuckled. "I just couldn't concentrate on Democratic women. I mean, I needed love. I think it was Woody Allen that said the good thing about being bisexual, it doubles your chances of getting a date. Well, I couldn't go — I wasn't that! I couldn't get that far, so I decided 'Well, I'll start dating Republicans. That'll double my chances to get a date, you know.' Some of it is just, you know, self-preservation."

CARVILLE WARNS DEMS NEED 'SOMEBODY THAT CAN WIN THIS GOD--- THING' WHEN ASKED IF AOC IS VIABLE FOR 2028

Democratic strategist James Carville has been married to former Republican strategist Mary Matalin for over 30 years. (Dave Bjerke/NBCU Photo Bank)

Carville offered a message to young progressives like Ocasio-Cortez when it comes to dating.

"Get over your preening and your moral superiority," Carville said. "And the more pragmatic in how you approach life, you'll end up being a lot happier, and you'll actually win an election. And therefore, you can actually do things, and you could do some of the things that you want, because if you lose, it doesn't do any good. It's about nothing. That's what I would tell them."

Joseph A. Wulfsohn is a media reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to joseph.wulfsohn@fox.com and on Twitter: @JosephWulfsohn.

articles.title: Massive World Trade Center steel beam arrives at West Point, uniting 9/11 heroes with generation sent to war
articles.excerpt: Army Col. Dan Steuwe recalls the bond between first responders and service members after Sept. 11, while Kelly Heffner describes the emotion of touching steel recovered from the World Trade Center. (C...
articles.body_text:
Army Col. Dan Steuwe recalls the bond between first responders and service members after Sept. 11, while Kelly Heffner describes the emotion of touching steel recovered from the World Trade Center. (Courtesy Tunnel to Towers)

A 21-foot steel beam recovered from the South Tower of the World Trade Center arrived at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point Tuesday, bringing a physical piece of the Sept. 11 attacks to the institution that trained generations of Army officers who would go on to serve in the wars that followed.

The 16,900-pound beam was brought to West Point as part of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation’s Steel Across America tour, a nationwide commemoration marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks. Tuesday’s ceremony was the tour’s 33rd stop.

West Point Superintendent Lt. Gen. James B. Bartholomees III said the steel connects the courage shown by first responders on 9/11 with the Americans who answered the call to serve in the years that followed.

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, this piece of steel reminds us of the courage of first responders like Stephen Siller and the countless Americans who answered the call in the years that followed, including generations of West Point graduates," Bartholomees said. "Today, young men and women continue that legacy of service, guided by Duty, Honor, Country."

9/11 STEEL BEAM ARRIVES AT FLORIDA SCHOOL WHERE BUSH LEARNED AMERICA WAS UNDER ATTACK

New York State Police and other first responders gather around a piece of World Trade Center steel during the Steel Across America tour's stop at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The ceremony brought together cadets, faculty, staff and guests and opened with a color guard and Pipes & Drums procession by members of the NYPD, FDNY and Port Authority Police Department. The program also included the national anthem, an invocation and blessing of the steel, and a moment of reflection accompanied by "Amazing Grace."

BENJAMIN HALL TACKLES GRUELING ONE WORLD TRADE CENTER CLIMB ON PROSTHETIC LEGS TO HONOR FALLEN HEROES

Army personnel and Frank Siller view a steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center's South Tower during its stop at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

Frank Siller, chairman and CEO of Tunnel to Towers and the brother of fallen FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller, recalled his brother’s final actions on Sept. 11.

"Twenty-five years ago, my brother Stephen strapped on 60 pounds of gear and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel toward danger, duty, and the people who needed him inside those towers," Siller said.

9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

New York State Police members stand in front of a 21-foot steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center's South Tower during a Tunnel to Towers event at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

"Duty, Honor, Country: those values connect West Point cadets, Stephen, and first responders all across this country," he continued. "We are grateful to West Point for welcoming us, and we leave more committed than ever to making sure the sacrifice of September 11 is never forgotten."

According to Tunnel to Towers, Stephen Siller was off duty when the attacks began and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel carrying 60 pounds of gear toward the World Trade Center, where he died while responding to the attacks.

FOX NATION, TUNNEL TO TOWERS EXPLORES HOW AMERICA’S PASTIME HELPED A GRIEVING NEW YORK HEAL AFTER 9/11

First responders at West Point gather around a 16,900-pound steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center's South Tower. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The foundation created in his memory provides mortgage-free homes to Gold Star and fallen first responder families with young children, builds specially adapted smart homes for catastrophically injured veterans and first responders, and works to address veteran homelessness.

For some of those gathered around the beam Tuesday, its arrival at West Point carried a personal connection between the first responders who rushed toward the towers and the service members who deployed overseas in the years that followed.

9/11 MUSEUM TO OFFER FREE ADMISSION FOR VETERANS AHEAD OF MEMORIAL DAY WEEKEND

Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller attends a ceremony marking the arrival of World Trade Center steel at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

Col. Dan Steuwe of the U.S. Army recalled an image that he said many soldiers in his platoon carried with them after 9/11 as they went overseas.

"There was a cartoon character that a lot of the soldiers in my platoon carried with us after 9-11 as we went overseas," Steuwe said. "It was one of the firemen handing off the American flag to a service member coming out of the rubble of the towers."

Steuwe described the image as another symbol of the unity between first responders and service members "serving something greater than ourselves and protecting this country."

Kelly Heffner, who is listed by Tunnel to Towers along with her husband, Tom Heffner, as a supporter and corporate sponsor, became emotional after approaching the South Tower beam.

"To touch that beam, there’s an energy with it and it brings you back and it — you know that you can never forget," Heffner said.

The artifact's stop at West Point comes nearly 25 years after the attacks sent a generation of American service members to Afghanistan, Iraq and other theaters during the war on terror.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller speaks during the Steel Across America tour's stop at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

Bartholomees later joined Siller to receive a commemorative steel flag on behalf of West Point. The custom-built piece features the New York City skyline and Twin Towers and incorporates World Trade Center steel. According to Tunnel to Towers, the flag is presented to people and institutions that have demonstrated a commitment to the foundation’s mission.

After the formal program, attendees were invited to approach the beam and spend time reflecting beside the steel.

The Steel Across America tour is scheduled to continue Thursday at the Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

articles.title: Falcons' Tua Tagovailoa gets roasted on social media after allegedly commenting on his own post
articles.excerpt: Former NFL QB Brian Hoyer joins Danny Parkins and Coach Eric Mangini to discuss Deshaun Watson getting the Week 1 start for the Cleveland Browns, whether Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears can start...
articles.body_text:
Former NFL QB Brian Hoyer joins Danny Parkins and Coach Eric Mangini to discuss Deshaun Watson getting the Week 1 start for the Cleveland Browns, whether Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears can start the season hot, and who should get the starting nod for the Atlanta Falcons: Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr.

Tua Tagovailoa’s latest errant pass came in the comments section of his recent Instagram post.

The 28-year-old quarterback posted six pictures on social media of him with the Atlanta Falcons and captioned the post, "For the A" with a salute emoji. However, his mishap came in the comments section.

The quarterback appeared to comment on his own post, "We’re so proud of you!! You got this," with a heart emoji. The comment was deleted, and then his wife took to the comments section and posted a strikingly similar message.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons looks to pass against the Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Fla., on Aug. 28, 2026. (Carmen Mandato/Getty Images)

"We are so proud of you! You got this!!" Annah posted with a heart emoji. The only difference between the comment from Tua’s account and Annah’s was the number of exclamation points.

While the comment was quickly deleted, the internet caught the mistake and roasted the quarterback for the mishap.

"Not even trying to hide the self-love is hilarious," one user wrote on X.

"Tua forgetting the burner is comedy gold," another posted on X.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa passes against the Miami Dolphins during the first half of an NFL preseason football game Friday, Aug. 28, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Fla. (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

"Oh brother this guy STINKS," someone else posted on X.

Another called the message of self-support "His Daily Affirmations."

OutKick reached out to Tagovailoa’s representatives for comment but did not immediately get a response.

Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons recovers his own fumble against the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of an NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Aug. 14, 2026, in Atlanta, Ga. (Getty Images)

Tagovailoa signed a one-year contract with the Falcons after being released by the Miami Dolphins to compete with Michael Penix Jr. for the starting quarterback job. Tagovailoa seemed to have an inside track toward the starting job with Penix’s training camp debut delayed because of his recovery from a torn ACL.

Tagovailoa has reportedly struggled in training camp, leaving the door open for Penix to take the job.

However, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has not yet named a Week 1 starting quarterback for the team’s matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The team carried four quarterbacks on its initial roster, with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand also on the roster.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: US strikes Iran as state media reports four killed at wedding party
articles.excerpt:
Vessels were visible across the Strait of Hormuz from Oman this week

American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command has said in a statement.

The Iranian Red Crescent sai...
articles.body_text:
Vessels were visible across the Strait of Hormuz from Oman this week

American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command has said in a statement.

The Iranian Red Crescent said four people including a young child were killed, and more than 50 injured, when shrapnel from a US missile attack hit a home where a wedding celebration was taking place in Sirik in southern Iran.

Centcom said the strikes followed "recent attempted attacks" by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and "American service members deployed to the region".

The IRGC said the US would regret the strikes, and Iranian news agencies reported that retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US targets had begun.

Donald Trump, when the US strikes were announced on Tuesday afternoon, warned that Iran would be hit again at "a much harder and higher level" if it retaliated.

The attack follows the first known US strikes on Iran since late July earlier this week, when forces attacked two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles at air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE.

Centcom said US forces had begun striking IRGC targets at 12:00 ET (16:00 GMT).

As well as the Sirik attack, other reports said projectiles had hit the areas of Chabahar and Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, and that explosions were heard in Qeshm island and Bandar Abbas.

The IRGC was reported as saying it had launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Jordan's Aqaba in retaliation for the Sirik attack.

The Jordanian Armed Forces said there were no deaths or injuries as a result of the attack from Iran, according to the country's state-affiliated Al-Mamlaka network.

The network also said that the country's national security centre had warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governates of falling debris, adding that the warning had since ended.

Trump said Tuesday's "large and powerful" strikes were a response to Iran's targeting of a US military base in Jordan, adding the country had "failed" at adding sea mines to the Strait.

He also threatened that a much larger-scale attack was "waiting in the wings".

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic.

A US-Iran agreement, known as the Memorandum of Understanding, to extend a ceasefire between the two countries was signed in June.

However that agreement has expired, leading to a resumption of hostilities. Both the US and Iran have also fired on shipping, with Tehran targeting vessels it says have sought to cross the Strait without its permission and the US enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Washington also announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies.

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

However on Tuesday Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was quoted by state media as saying if the US returned to committing to the agreement, Iran would reciprocate.

articles.title: News live: Five Australians confirmed safe after Nepal-Tibet flooding; Chanel Contos urges action on ‘manosphere’
articles.excerpt:
Package steps up support to fight transnational drug trafficking flowing through the Pacific. Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Five Australians ...
articles.body_text:
Package steps up support to fight transnational drug trafficking flowing through the Pacific. Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Five Australians have been confirmed safe in the devastating Nepal floods, meaning the number of unaccounted-for citizens has been revised from 43 missing on Tuesday morning to 38.

Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, one in China and three outside the crisis-hit area.

These Australians had not spoken to families and next of kin since the disaster struck seven days ago.

Dfat has received nearly 800 calls in relation to the floods, with 18 Australian personnel having travelled to Nepal to join staff on the ground.

More humanitarian and disaster relief from Australia is due to arrive in Nepal this afternoon.

Allegra Spender says government has an ‘opportunity’ to make social media safer with opt-in algorithms

Independent MP Allegra Spender said the Australia government has an “opportunity” to make social media algorithms safer for all Australians, not just young people.

The government is considering the change, saying social media was playing a “huge role” in the increase in sexual violence among teenagers and choking. Chanel Contos’s Teach Us Consent has campaigned for tech giants’ algorithms to be opt-in only.

double quotation markWhat we see is that the algorithms as they are currently running, in certain circumstances, can serve content that has real damaging effects potentially across our community. And so I think creating an opt-in for people to make the default of social media safer and to give people really active choice in relation to social media makes a lot of sense.

The MP went on to say the under-16s social media ban was “not really working” and there was still a lot of work to do to see if the ban could be more effective:

double quotation markLet’s be honest that the challenges of social media don’t stop when you’re 16. You know, many adults struggle with … particularly the addictive nature of social media. And at the same time, we know that some of those issues that both Asio has highlighted and also the misogynistic content don’t just stop when you’re 16.

Five Australians have been confirmed safe in the devastating Nepal floods, meaning the number of unaccounted-for citizens has been revised from 43 missing on Tuesday morning to 38.

Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, one in China and three outside the crisis-hit area.

These Australians had not spoken to families and next of kin since the disaster struck seven days ago.

Dfat has received nearly 800 calls in relation to the floods, with 18 Australian personnel having travelled to Nepal to join staff on the ground.

More humanitarian and disaster relief from Australia is due to arrive in Nepal this afternoon.

Drug testing to resume at NSW music festivals

Drug testing will resume at New South Wales music festivals from October, but will not be rolled out into the wider community despite calls from peak health and harm reduction groups.

On Wednesday the state government announced NSW Health will consult with the music festival industry and harm reduction organisations to roll out pill testing at up to 15 music festivals each year.

There will be no change to the use of sniffer dogs at music festivals, a government spokesperson confirmed, which have been found to prompt risky drug taking.

Good morning, everyone. Nick Visser here to take over. Let’s dive in.

Australia will step up its support to fight transnational drug trafficking flowing through the Pacific, with a $600m package.

Anthony Albanese announced the new investment at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, which aims to stop the contraband arriving in Australia.

The increase in drug flow across the Pacific is a huge problem in several countries: linked to increased gang activity in Samoa and Tonga, and a sharp rise in the HIV rate in Fiji.

Heightened activity is showing up in Australian Federal Police interventions of narcotics in the region.

In 2025, about 4.6 tonnes of illicit drugs were seized by local and international law enforcement, the Australian Federal Police reported.

In the first five months of this year, 17 tonnes have been picked up – mostly cocaine.

The new package – which will be opt-in for Pacific countries – will include enhanced aerial surveillance, and police and border training.

“Drug trafficking is having a devastating impact on Pacific communities,” Pacific minister Pat Conroy said.

“This initiative responds to the calls of regional leaders to do more, and to step up regional coordination to address this scourge.”

Consent education advocate Chanel Contos will urge Australia to enforce a social media opt-in algorithm to help reduce the influence of the “manosphere” on both men and women.

Contos will deliver a speech about the harms of social media algorithms in Australia in an address to the National Press Club in Canberra at midday.

double quotation markThis is crucial, and the detail in any reform will determine its success – as will be the overall strength of the proposed Digital Duty of Care reforms that are needed in their own right. It is too easy for Big Tech to design schemes that appear as structural reform but actually suit them just fine.

The Teach Us Consent CEO will point to examples of algorithmic harms such as the “manosphere”, accusing bad actors of jumping on to “a market opportunity” that has misogyny “at the heart of its business model”.

double quotation markIt usually starts with something as harmless as a workout video, or motivational content. Very quickly, boys and men are taken into the “manosphere”, communities that persistently promote the idea that emotional control, material wealth, and physical appearance and dominance, especially over women, are markers of male worth.

This is harmful to the individual man consuming this content, and then anyone else close to him in life, including other men, but disproportionately women and girls.

Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it’ll be Nick Visser with the main action.

articles.title: Urgent need for access to Iranian sites, cautions UN nuclear watchdog
articles.excerpt:
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has called for “utmost urgency” to address the lack of access to Iran’s nuclear sites.

In a quarterly report seen by news agencies on Tuesday, the United...
articles.body_text:
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has called for “utmost urgency” to address the lack of access to Iran’s nuclear sites.

In a quarterly report seen by news agencies on Tuesday, the United Nations nuclear watchdog labelled its “lack of information about this nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of proliferation concern”.

The US has claimed preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon – an ambition that Tehran continues to deny – as the motivation for the war that it launched in March. However, Tehran has been successful in shifting the focus of the hostilities to control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz waterway.

In particular, the IAEA report raised concerns over the lack of access to the Isfahan plant, which was targeted several times by the US and Israel over the past year or so.

In the report, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi expressed his “conviction that the long-standing problems and recurrent crises surrounding these issues must be resolved through a long-lasting, verifiable diplomatic agreement”.

However, Iran has said that access to the sites that have been struck by military action must be arranged via special arrangement.

The head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organization, Mohammad Eslami, said on August 26 that the IAEA “cannot seek to inspect these centres until it develops specific criteria and protocols for inspecting sites targeted by military attacks”.

Tehran suspended cooperation with the UN nuclear watchdog following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites before saying in September 2025 it would allow the UN agency’s inspectors to return.

However, access to the nuclear sites that have been bombed has not yet been granted. Despite US President Donald Trump having claimed last year that the US had destroyed the facilities and crippled Tehran’s nuclear programme, Iran’s stores of enriched uranium remain unaccounted for.

Tehran has repeatedly denied any military ambition linked to its nuclear programme, insisting on its right to the technology for civilian purposes.

However, the IAEA, whose latest report will be discussed at its board of governors meeting from September 21-25, has reported in the past that the level of Iran’s enrichment of its uranium reserves is well above that needed for civilian purposes, although neither is it at the level of weapons grade.

articles.title: Bank of America executive identified as victim of stabbing in Times Square
articles.excerpt:
Erin Piacenti, a 32-year-old vice-president at the bank, was killed in Tuesday stabbing in New York City, officials say

A corporate vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing in New Y...
articles.body_text:
Erin Piacenti, a 32-year-old vice-president at the bank, was killed in Tuesday stabbing in New York City, officials say

A corporate vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing in New York City’s Times Square, the second-biggest US lending bank ⁠said on Tuesday about a ⁠random incident that took place ​in broad daylight in the bustling heart of Manhattan.

The incident had brought the streets of the crowded area to a halt on Monday as emergency vehicles swarmed between the skyscrapers.

The ⁠deceased was Erin Piacenti, 32, according to the New York City police department (NYPD). Bank of America confirmed the loss of a staff member. Piacenti was a vice-⁠president in the bank’s business selection and conflicts unit, according to her LinkedIn profile.

“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. ​She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. ‌Our hearts go out to her ‌family and all of her loved ones,” the US banking company said in a statement on Tuesday. Bank of America’s Manhattan office ‌is located a stone’s throw from Times Square, at One Bryant Park.

Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.

An unnamed 68-year-old man also suffered stab wounds in the attack and was in stable condition, the NYPD said in a statement.

Jessica Tisch, the NYPD’s commissioner, said Monday afternoon’s attack near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue, appeared to be random and unprovoked.

The NYPD said when officers arrived on the scene they found Pamela Cisneros, a 49-year-old woman, who was brandishing two large knives and advanced toward ‌officers, who used a stun gun but were unable to persuade her to drop the weapons. Officers shot Cisneros and she was later pronounced dead. Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history.

Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of global corporate and investment banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” ​in an internal memo seen by Reuters.

“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote. “Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”

Koder said that Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.

Reuters and the Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: Florida set to execute 14th person this year with two more execution dates set
articles.excerpt:
Harold Gene Lucas, 74, was convicted of killing a 16-year-old girl who rejected his advances and wounding her two friends

A Florida man convicted of killing a 16-year-old girl who rejected his romant...
articles.body_text:
Harold Gene Lucas, 74, was convicted of killing a 16-year-old girl who rejected his advances and wounding her two friends

A Florida man convicted of killing a 16-year-old girl who rejected his romantic advances and wounding two of her friends was set to be executed Tuesday evening.

Harold Gene Lucas, 74, was scheduled to receive a three-drug injection starting at 6pm at Florida state prison near Starke. He was sentenced to die for the 1976 fatal shooting of Jill Piper and the wounding of her friends, Richard Byrd Jr and Terri Rice.

Lucas would be the 14th prisoner put to death in Florida this year, and Ron DeSantis, the Republican governor, has already signed death warrants for two more execution dates later this month. Lucas chose not to file any last-ditch court appeals, telling a judge after his death warrant was issued, that he wanted to waive all post-conviction proceedings.

“I’ve been on death row for 50 years, and I have no desire to carry this any further,” Lucas told the judge, according to court transcripts. “The sooner it’s over, the better I’ll enjoy it. I am tired.”

On Tuesday, Lucas awoke at 545am and was later visited by his sister and given a meal of steak and fries, Department of Corrections spokesman Jordan Kirkland said. Lucas did not meet with a spiritual adviser, Kirkland added at an afternoon news briefing.

Lucas was sentenced to death – and resentenced to death four more times – after being convicted of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted first-degree murder for the attack.

According to court records, Lucas was 24 in August 1976 when he was arrested for trespassing at Piper’s Bonita Springs home, south of Fort Myers. Lucas had known the teen for four years and worked for her family, officials said. Lucas and Piper had previously dated and Lucas told a friend he planned to marry Piper.

About a week after the arrest, Lucas and Piper had two separate confrontations on the same day, several hours apart, investigators said. Witnesses testified Lucas threatened to kill Piper.

Piper asked Byrd and Rice to spend that night at her home for protection, officials said. Lucas eventually showed up with a rifle and shot Piper multiple times while she begged for her life and then shot and wounded her friends, investigators said. Lucas was arrested the next day.

Lucas was initially sentenced to death in 1977 with a 12-0 jury recommendation, court records show. The Florida supreme court later ruled the trial judge was wrong to consider the heinousness of the attempted murders while deciding the sentence for the murder. That same trial judge resentenced Lucas to death in 1980.

By the time a third sentencing was ordered, the original trial judge had died and a new judge was assigned. That judge sentenced Lucas to death in 1985, but the Florida supreme court later ruled a new jury should hear the case, though the conviction itself would still stand. The new jury recommended death by 11-1, and Lucas was sentenced to death for a fourth time in 1987. The Florida supreme court ruled that sentencing order wasn’t clear, and Lucas was sentenced to death for a final time in 1990.

A total of 47 people were executed in the US in 2025. Florida led the way with 19 lethal injections, a record in the state since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976.

Florida has carried out more than half of the 23 total executions in the US this year. In July, Florida executed two prisoners in one day, the first state in nearly a decade to do so.

Two more Florida executions are planned this month, that of Daniel Owen Conahan Jr, 72, on 10 September, and Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, on 29 September.

Conahan was convicted of kidnapping and strangling a man he had paid to pose for nude photos, and authorities suspect him of similar homicides committed in the 1990s in south-west Florida. Beasley was convicted of beating a woman to death with a hammer, robbing her and stealing her car in 1995.

All Florida executions are carried out via lethal injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart, according to the department of corrections.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick is right about the NFL's 'performative' racism campaign — but he's also a hypocrite
articles.excerpt: "So he has serious domestic violence allegations against him, Josh Jacob does. And where is the national sports media outrage? Where is it? In fact, the freaking NFL, instead of end racism and it take...
articles.body_text:
"So he has serious domestic violence allegations against him, Josh Jacob does. And where is the national sports media outrage? Where is it? In fact, the freaking NFL, instead of end racism and it takes all of that bull*hit should say 'end domestic violence' in its end zones instead of this nonsense. No, our backwards *ss, stupid *ss liberal sports media would rather get all over Jackson Dart because, well, he introduced the president."

As part of an ongoing media blitz to promote his upcoming memoir, former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick dismissed the league’s condemnation of racism as "performative."

In an interview with NBC News, Kaepernick criticized NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell over a video he released in 2020 amid nationwide protests following George Floyd’s death.

"His response through that video was only because of pressure from players, not because it was altruistic," Kaepernick said.

COLIN KAEPERNICK TO RECEIVE MUHAMMAD ALI AWARD FOR FIGHTING 'RACIAL INJUSTICE'

In the video, Goodell said the NFL condemned "racism and the systematic oppression of Black people."

"[Goodell’s message was] so laughable, in my mind, and so disingenuous," Kaepernick continued. "We had been trying to address the issue that the NFL created with blackballing me for years. To come out and say we should have listened on the back of that — while I’m still actively trying to play in the NFL — it’s so performative."

Colin Kaepernick speaks onstage during The Gordon Parks Foundation Awards Dinner and Auction 2026 at Cipriani 42nd Street on May 19, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for The Gordon Parks Foundation)

The NFL’s social justice campaigns and messaging are performative. Painting "End Racism" in the end zones and approving "Black Lives Matter" on helmets were ways for the league to signal its virtue. They were public-relations decisions, perhaps even financial ones, designed to avoid potential backlash from sponsors and consumers.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES 'RACIST NFL' CLAIM, CONTINUES DEFENDING COLIN KAEPERNICK

The fact that Goodell, or anyone else, felt obligated to announce that the NFL does not support racism and the systematic oppression of black people perfectly exemplifies the term "performative."

That said, Kaepernick is not the one to lecture anyone about fraudulent behavior.

Colin Kaepernick, No. 7 of the San Francisco 49ers kneels for the national anthem before a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Levi's Stadium on Oct. 23, 2016, in Santa Clara, Calif. (Getty Images)

The former quarterback has spent the past decade performing, pandering, and spreading propaganda. His entire claim to activism is fraudulent.

Most notably, Kaepernick participated in a Netflix docuseries in which he compared the NFL scouting combine to a slave auction.

"Before they put you on the field, teams poke, prod, and examine you. Searching for any defect that might affect your performance," Kaepernick narrated in Colin in Black & White. "No boundary respected. No dignity left intact. What they don't want you to understand is what's being established is a power dynamic."

The scene then shifts to one in which players transform into enslaved black men in shackles while white slave masters bid on them and whip them.

Eli Harold #58, Colin Kaepernick #7 and Eric Reid #35 of the San Francisco 49ers kneel in protest on the sideline, during the anthem, prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at New Era Field on Oct. 16, 2016 in Orchard Park, New York. (Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Kaepernick continued trying to return to the NFL, despite comparing the process of entering the league to slavery. Imagine that.

He is no more honest than Goodell or the sports media figures who championed his campaign.

Kaepernick has not played in the NFL since 2016. He later filed a grievance accusing the league and its owners of colluding to keep him out. The case was settled in 2019, with neither side admitting wrongdoing.
