articles.title: Houston mayor says his city is a better location than Austin for an NHL expansion franchise
articles.excerpt: After a strong round of expansion over the last decade, bringing in the Vegas Golden Knights, Seattle Kraken and Utah Mammoth (who are considered an expansion team; confusing, I know), the NHL is look...
articles.body_text:
After a strong round of expansion over the last decade, bringing in the Vegas Golden Knights, Seattle Kraken and Utah Mammoth (who are considered an expansion team; confusing, I know), the NHL is looking to grow again.

The league wants to add two more clubs, one of which will be based in Texas. The question is whether it will be Houston or Austin joining the league.

Now, Houston's mayor is making his case for why his city is the best option for the league.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Houston Mayor John Whitmire gave some reasons why his city is more cut out for an NHL team than Austin is. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images for Houston Hispanic Chamber of Commerce)

Both cities offer upsides. For Austin, the league has a chance to be the first of the four major leagues to set up shop there, a strategy that worked well in Las Vegas.

However, Houston is currently the biggest media market in the nation without an NHL team, something NHL Deputy Commissioner Bill Daly recently confirmed is a big factor in the decision.

"We're ready. In fact, we're talking to multiple parties that are interested," Mayor John Whitmire said in an interview with The Sporting News. "So when we get a proposal, if the city can do something to a system, we'll be there. We'll definitely be a better location than Austin."

Gordie, Marty, and Mark Howe played for the WHA's Houston Aeros in the 1970s. (Bettmann / Contributor)

Houston has never had an NHL team, but was home to the World Hockey Association's Houston Aeros in the 1970s. Since then, it has been home to some minor league teams, as has Austin.

STANLEY CUP FINAL RATINGS SHOW OLYMPIC HOCKEY FEVER IS ALIVE AND WELL IN THE UNITED STATES

"I think [the NHL] would never regret it if they gave a franchise to Houston. They'd never regret it," Whitmire said. "Austin is a great city, but it's not Houston... If you talk to the sports franchises in town, I think they'd tell you we're great partners."

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson's office has not replied to a request for comment on Whitmire's remarks.

Either Houston (pictured) or Austin will bet getting an NHL team, the league's second in Texas. (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images)

While the two Lone Star State cities battle it out for Club No. 33, some cities are still angling for Club No. 34.

Atlanta is routinely coming up as a top destination, which would be the third time the league has put a team there. It's a large media market, and there are currently two competing arena projects in the works in the city's suburbs.

articles.title: Dan Le Batard thinks there are too many white NFL analysts, despite the racial makeup of his own company
articles.excerpt:
Dan Le Batard is unhappy with the racial makeup of NFL analysts on television. He says there are too many white analysts and not enough black ones for his liking.

"Luke Kuechly is now the up-and-comi...
articles.body_text:
Dan Le Batard is unhappy with the racial makeup of NFL analysts on television. He says there are too many white analysts and not enough black ones for his liking.

"Luke Kuechly is now the up-and-coming broadcasting star that people like. When they look at Tony Romo and they put him on the bench for a while, they replace him with J.J. Watt," Le Batard said on his podcast. "[Rob Gronkowski] has a job, even though Gronk is a notoriously bad talker. I just wonder if you guys notice that the sport is disproportionately black, and the broadcasters that get hired are disproportionately white, and it’s on purpose. I’m asking the question. It’s to make it palatable to the broadest section of people."

He continued, asking his co-hosts and listeners to, at least, notice the whiteness on air.

"I’m just asking if you guys notice that all of the up-and-coming people are always the white guys. There aren’t that many white stars in football. There are plenty of black stars. Why are the white ones the only ones who get the broadcasting jobs?… I’m just wondering whether people notice. It’s always J.J. Watt. It’s always Luke Kuechly. As if there aren’t a bunch of Jonathan Vilmas out there that are available."

Dan LeBatard arrives at Shaq's Fun House at Mana Wynwood Convention Center in Miami, Fla., on Jan. 31, 2020. (Getty Images)

JEMELE HILL POSTS MISLEADING STUDY TO SUGGEST THERE ARE TOO MANY 'WHITE MEN' IN SPORTS MEDIA

Imagine hosting a sports show and choosing that as your topic on Sept. 1, just days before the start of the college football season and a week before the NFL season.

For background, Le Batard has spent much of the past year complaining about the number of white people he sees on television. More on that later.

Not only is Le Batard pandering, but his gripe is also invalid. He cherry-picked a few media hires while ignoring many others.

Le Batard pointed to the promotions of Kuechly and Watt. Notice how he ignored ESPN adding Jason McCourty to Monday Night Countdown, the pregame show that will serve as bumper programming for the Super Bowl this season. He also neglected to mention that McCourty’s brother, Devin, is now a halftime analyst at NBC.

CBS elevated Charles Davis to its lead college football game analyst role this offseason. Fox Sports recently added Robert Griffin III to its color-commentator lineup. Le Batard mentioned neither move.

What’s more, the majority of NFL analysts at ESPN are black. Dan Orlovsky is the only full-time white NFL analyst who contributes daily across various programs.

ESPN’s featured NFL analysts include Orlovsky, Mina Kimes, an Asian woman, and several black former players, including McCourty, Marcus Spears, Chris Canty, Andrew Hawkins, Louis Riddick, Sam Acho and Booger McFarland.

We could continue. In fact, we could not find a major sports network where white NFL analysts outnumber black ones.

DAN LE BATARD DEMANDS THE MEDIA MAKE JAXSON DART 'UNCOMFORTABLE' FOR INTRODUCING TRUMP

A general view of the ESPN Monday Night Countdown booth before the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cincinnati Bengals at EverBank Stadium on Dec. 4, 2023, in Jacksonville, Fla. (Getty Images)

So which network is Le Batard referring to and shaming? OutKick asked him that exact question Tuesday:

"Dan, did you count the number of white vs. black NFL analysts in the industry? If not, why did you make a false claim that networks ‘disproportionately’ hire white ones over black?

"I just looked at the rosters of ESPN, Fox, CBS and NBC. There are far more black NFL analysts than white ones."

Notice that we did not include Meadowlark Media, the sports media company Le Batard owns and operates. It turns out Meadowlark is one company in which black people appear to be underrepresented on air.

Meadowlark’s NFL show is hosted by Dave Dameshek, a white man. Other hosts on the network include David Samson, Brendan Hunt, Rebecca Lowe, Anthony Curcio and Jessica Smetana. All of them are, wait for it, white.

The only non-white host we could find was Pablo Torre, who is Asian.

RYAN CLARK MADE IT TOO DIFFICULT FOR ESPN TO JUSTIFY KEEPING HIM AFTER YEARS OF CONTROVERSY

We asked Le Batard about the lack of black analysts and hosts at his network. We will update the story if he responds.

But do not count on it. We also asked Le Batard about a previous comment he made on a similar topic. In July, he criticized ESPN for not putting any black faces in positions of leadership.

"You’re gonna have a network run by McAfee and all of the white people now in charge there," Le Batard said about ESPN after the network fired Ryan Clark, whom he referred to as a "proud black man."

As we noted at the time, Le Batard’s company also lacks black leadership and is made up mostly, you guessed it, of white people.

He did not provide an explanation for his hypocrisy. Nor did he explain why he criticized the UFC for retaining Dana White, seen on video slapping his wife after she slapped him, and then apologizing, while employing Howard Bryant, who was arrested for allegedly beating and choking his wife.

Ryan Clark of ESPN's Monday Night Football Countdown before the NFC Wild Card Playoff game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on Jan. 13, 2025, in Glendale, Ariz. (Getty Images)

In sum, unless your workforce properly represents Bluesky’s preferred demographics, you best not get into the business of counting the skin colors of employees at a particular company. You will likely end up looking like a hypocrite yourself.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

No serious person is that concerned about the racial breakdown of the people breaking down NFL games.

He is pandering. He's race-baiting to appease the people who shamed him for his previous juvenile lifestyle, while quietly surrounding himself with mostly white men.

articles.title: Ex-Indiana deputy charged with felony for allegedly using Flock cameras to stalk girlfriend
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Danamarie McNicholl has the latest on police officers across the country being arrested for allegedly misusing Flock Safety camera systems, as growing concerns over privacy and ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Danamarie McNicholl has the latest on police officers across the country being arrested for allegedly misusing Flock Safety camera systems, as growing concerns over privacy and accountability fuel scrutiny of the license plate reader technology and its use by law enforcement agencies nationwide on 'America Reports.'

A former Indiana sheriff's deputy has been charged in connection with abusing access to Flock camera technology to stalk his girlfriend for over a year by allegedly conducting more than 2,000 searches for her license plate.

Skylar Thompson, 31, faces one count of official misconduct as a Level 6 felony and a misdemeanor count of fraud.

The Jackson County Sheriff’s Department discovered that Thompson used the Flock technology to conduct the searches between Dec. 31, 2025, and Aug. 2, during an internal audit of the system, the Jackson County Prosecutor's Office said.

POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN'

Skylar Thompson, 31, a former Indiana sheriff's deputy, is charged in connection with allegedly conducting more than 2,000 searches for the same license plate using Flock cameras, prosecutors said. (Getty Images; Jackson County Prosecutor's Office)

Thompson reportedly listed his searches as "city planning/traffic analysis" despite never being assigned duties involving either duty, prosecutors said.

The agency then asked the Indiana State Police to investigate. Thompson turned himself in to authorities Monday.

He resigned from the sheriff's department the day he was confronted about the alleged abuse. He also drove to his then-girlfriend's home and admitted what he had done, WKBN-TV reported.

FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES

Flock cameras are used in towns across the nation as license plate readers, but the technology has come under scrutiny in recent months. (Lori Van Buren/Albany Times Union via Getty Images, File)

"Law enforcement officers are entrusted with access to sensitive information and investigative tools, and that access must be used responsibly and only for legitimate law enforcement purposes," the Jackson County Prosecutor’s Office said. "No person is above the law, including those entrusted with enforcing it."

Flock cameras have come under heavy scrutiny over privacy concerns and the potential for misuse.

Flock Safety spokesperson Paris Lewbel defended the technology as an important public safety tool in a statement to Fox News Digital last month.

"Flock’s technology is an important public safety tool for law enforcement agencies across Texas, helping officers solve serious crimes, find missing people, recover stolen vehicles, and support safer communities," Lewbel said.

"We support thoughtful legislation and strong privacy, transparency, and accountability guardrails that ensure technology is used responsibly while preserving law enforcement’s ability to use effective tools to keep people safe," Lewbel continued.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Deported Milo Yiannopoulos says he is ‘ashamed’ of support for Trump
articles.excerpt:
British far-right pundit breaks silence on ICE arrest and deportation and says he was ‘really, really terrified’

Milo Yiannopoulos, the British far-right commentator who was arrested last week by Imm...
articles.body_text:
British far-right pundit breaks silence on ICE arrest and deportation and says he was ‘really, really terrified’

Milo Yiannopoulos, the British far-right commentator who was arrested last week by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers in Louisiana and deported to the United Kingdom, has broken his silence about the experience, saying that “for the first time I know what it feels like to be really, really terrified”.

Yiannopoulos on Tuesday appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored, a YouTube show presented by Piers Morgan, the British broadcaster and media personality. Yiannopoulos, 41, described the experience in the US as “humiliating and disorientating”, “physically degrading” and “frightening”.

He also said that he was “ashamed” of his previous support for Donald Trump, who has pursued an agenda of mass deportation throughout his second presidency.

“I didn’t really understand the physical reality of how institutionalized the brutality is in America” he said, adding: “It’s like everybody that’s arrested is an MS-13 gang member, and it hurts a lot more than it looks like on television.”

His remarks came just days after he was deported from the US, after being arrested on Thursday by ICE officers at New Orleans airport.

In a statement last week, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the parent agency of ICE, said Yiannopoulos had “legally entered the country” in May 2019, but “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.

Yiannopoulos was an early supporter of Trump before he first became US president in 2016. He is a former editor of Breitbart News and later worked to help the rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, explore a presidential run in 2024.

The homeland security department said Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an immigration judge on 22 July “after failing to show up for his immigration hearing”.

In the Piers Morgan interview, Yiannopoulos disputed the government’s account and denied previously overstaying a visa. He said he is married to an American, and claimed he held a green card that he was “renewing on a two-year basis”.

The Guardian has contacted homeland security and the White House for comment on Yiannopoulos’s remarks.

Yiannopoulos also said that while he was detained, “no one would tell me anything” – a common complaint from people held in ICE custody.

“I don’t think I’ve ever been frightened like that before” he told Morgan. “I think maybe in the past I’ve been a little bit blasé when people talked about their trauma, a little bit cavalier when people talked about stuff kind of lingering with them, but I get it now … I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.”

Last year, in posts on social media, Yiannopoulos had been supportive of Trump’s crackdown on immigration.

In one post, he wrote: “There is one concrete thing we must insist on this administration delivering. It matters a lot more than debts measured in imaginary money. We have got to deport millions and millions and millions of people. Without that, nothing else matters.”

In another post, Yiannopoulos had said that California “needs ICE checkpoints at supermarket entrances, gas stations, strip malls, intersections and government buildings, with on the spot deportation for anyone who can’t prove they are in the US legally”.

During Tuesday’s interview, Yiannopoulos said of his past support for Trump: “If I had any clue that anything remotely like this was even possible, I would never have gotten involved in supporting Trump in the first place and I’m very ashamed that I did.”

articles.title: Briton among 119 more people rescued in Nepal after flash floods
articles.excerpt:
More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000 still missing in disaster triggered by glacial collapse

A British national was among 119 people rescued in Nepal on Tuesday, an official said...
articles.body_text:
More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000 still missing in disaster triggered by glacial collapse

A British national was among 119 people rescued in Nepal on Tuesday, an official said almost a week after deadly flash floods on the country’s border with Tibet.

An army spokesperson told reporters at a press conference that Tuesday’s rescue efforts had saved 118 Nepali nationals – 44 women and 74 men.

“We have also rescued one British male during this search and rescue operation, and the search and rescue operation is continuing,” he said.

The British man is yet to be identified. The UK Foreign Office was contacted for comment.

The rescues mark a rare breakthrough in a devastating week for Himalayan communities on both sides of the Nepal-Tibet border.

At least 1,050 people have been confirmed dead in Nepal since Wednesday’s flash floods, while Chinese state media said 66 people had been killed in Tibet. More than 4,000 people are still missing.

Nepal’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region. This included 330 foreign nationals, the Nepalese Tourist Board said in an update on Tuesday.

Preliminary analysis of satellite imagery suggests the collapse of a glacier high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the disaster.

The collapse – so large it was initially recorded as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake – triggered a deadly torrent of water, mud and ice that tore along the Lhende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on Wednesday.

Crews have faced dangerous and difficult conditions while searching unstable terrain and flood debris.

Search efforts are now focused on attempts to reach about 600 workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at several hydropower stations in the region.

“Massive work has been going on in the tunnel, all the tunnels,” the army spokesperson said on Tuesday.

Thirty-six British nationals are missing, the Foreign Office minister, Stewart Wood, told the House of Lords on Tuesday. The figure had previously been put at 33.

A rapid deployment rescue team from the UK arrived in Nepal on Saturday to provide support for Britons and their families as part of the government’s £5m commitment to support relief and recovery efforts.

The Red Cross estimates that 93,000 people have been directly affected by the disaster.

Scientists have said such disasters are more likely as the climate crisis affects mountainous and polar regions.

The UN’s top scientific advisory body said in 2023 that previously ice-bound landmasses – such as permafrost tundra and mountain glaciers – would become increasingly unstable as temperatures rose.

Officials from Nepal, China and Tibet met in May to discuss strengthening their joint response to floods, weather and glacier-related hazards, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

articles.title: Todd Haynes and Wallace Shawn among signatories of letter backing Mark Ruffalo amid antisemitism charge
articles.excerpt:
More than 170 Jewish artists, also including Joel Coen, Hannah Einbinder and Miranda July, have supported the actor after he criticized Paramount

A collective of more than 170 prominent Jewish artist...
articles.body_text:
More than 170 Jewish artists, also including Joel Coen, Hannah Einbinder and Miranda July, have supported the actor after he criticized Paramount

A collective of more than 170 prominent Jewish artists and academics – including Todd Haynes, Joel Coen, Miranda July, Hannah Einbinder, Wallace Shawn and Naomi Klein – have signed an open letter supporting Mark Ruffalo.

The actor had been accused of invoking antisemitic tropes after he criticized Paramount Skydance, the media company owned by David Ellison, a Donald Trump ally. Ruffalo had spoken out about the $111bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery (WBD).

In a statement posted to social media last week, the actor had highlighted the links between Paramount Skydance, poised to become one of the biggest media conglomerates in the US pending a court decision, and Oracle, the technology company owned by Ellison’s father, Larry, that has long supplied software to the Israel Defense Forces and government. Paramount responded to Ruffalo, saying it was “troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute”.

The letter, titled “Enough!”, dismisses the accusation against Ruffalo as part of an “outrageous smear campaign” and calls for the end to “the false and dangerous weaponization of charges of antisemitism against those who are brave enough to point out the obvious: that the assault on the Palestinian people and the assault on our liberties at home are deeply interconnected, and there is nothing antisemitic about recognizing that fact”.

“Calling Mark Ruffalo antisemitic because he is questioning a massive corporate merger is not only absurd – it’s a dangerous way to shut down legitimate criticism,” Ilana Glazer, the former Broad City star, said in an additional statement.

In his original post, Ruffalo shared a video of Safra Catz, former Oracle CEO and the current executive vice-chair, describing the “really profoundly scary technology” the company provided to Israel after the 7 October attack by Hamas in 2023. The actor accused Larry Ellison – who is worth an estimated $189bn and agreed to personally backstop $40.4bn in equity financing to help Paramount Skydance acquire WBD – of “using [Oracle] to fund his son David’s Warner Bros acquisition” and linked the software deals with the IDF to the merger that would unite two of the remaining five legacy studios in Hollywood, as well as a host of networks and news operations.

“These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you,” Ruffalo wrote.

Ruffalo urged his followers to oppose the merger, which he claimed would be “catastrophic” for the entertainment industry. In a separate statement after Paramount’s response, Ruffalo said: “Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract, or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people,” Ruffalo wrote. “This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel.”

The letter, whose signatories include Jewish artists, writers, creative professionals and faith leaders as well as several prominent Holocaust and genocide scholars, affirmed Ruffalo’s argument against the $111bn merger that already secured approval from the Trump administration in June: “The proposed merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery is no mere combination of two huge multinational companies. Yes, it will destroy thousands upon thousands of livelihoods. Yes, it will further consolidate the oligarchic control of our media (witness the gutting of CBS News). Yes, it will strangle competition and creativity in film and television production and distribution.

“But it will do all this and more as part of a larger project of tech-driven domination,” the letter continues, “a project Larry Ellison and his partners have never been shy about trumpeting – and one they themselves have explicitly linked to their support for the ongoing depredations being visited on the people of Palestine and their silencing of critics of those horrors.”

The letter cited the Trump-brokered sale of TikTok by the Chinese company ByteDance to US investors including Oracle; Larry Ellison’s reported $350m in personal funding of the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change amid the former prime minister’s ultimately unsuccessful bid, backed by Jared Kushner, to occupy a key position on Trump’s transitional board of peace for Gaza; and Oracle executives’ public backing of Israel’s military strikes in Gaza, “which has become an open-air laboratory for AI-driven killing and control technologies” celebrated by Catz and other Oracle officials.

“Pointing out the crucial connections between what is happening in Gaza and what is happening in Hollywood is the exact opposite of antisemitism,” the letter said. “It is, for us, the very essence of Jewish ethical duty.”

articles.title: Former PGA Tour star Hunter Mahan shares his thoughts on controversial Good Good ad, fallout that followed
articles.excerpt:
Six-time PGA Tour winner Hunter Mahan reacts to the controversial Good Good-Callaway golf ad, telling OutKick the "pendulum swung too far" amid the fallout.

Hunter Mahan, a six-time winner on the PGA...
articles.body_text:
Six-time PGA Tour winner Hunter Mahan reacts to the controversial Good Good-Callaway golf ad, telling OutKick the "pendulum swung too far" amid the fallout.

Hunter Mahan, a six-time winner on the PGA Tour, shares the opinion of the majority in the golf world on the controversial Good Good and Callaway golf ad and the fallout that continues to unfold: the advertisement was dumb, but the consequences that have followed seem too severe.

"Their impact on the game is huge, and with that size and scope of that lens on you, there is a responsibility, and I think they've realized that, probably in this ad and everything," Mahan told OutKick.

Good Good, the wildly popular YouTube channel and golf brand, teamed up with Callaway in late August and collaborated on a driver. To promote the new club, Good Good shared an advertisement in which co-founder Garrett Clark shoved a female member of the brand to the ground.

Garrett Clark walks along the 15th hole during the 2025 Tour Championship Creator Classic, presented by YouTube, prior to TOUR Championship, at East Lake Golf Club, on Aug. 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

THE SCOTTIE VS TIGER COMPARISON, MICHAEL BLOCK'S PARTY GETS SHUT DOWN, AND A FINAL WORD ON YOUTUBE GOLF DRAMA

After deleting the ad and sharing multiple apologetic statements, Callaway has cut ties with Good Good, the brand split with the PGA Tour ahead of its sponsored tournament set for November, and the brand's apparel has been pulled from the shelves at multiple retailers, among other ramifications.

"For as much as the ad is sort of silly, it's a terrible ad, I thought, and just in general kind of stupid, you're under a bigger lens now than when you were when you were just on YouTube," Mahan, the former No. 4 player in the world, explained. "I think they might have learned that lesson, and they maybe didn't realize who was watching and how people are going to be judging them, but like anything, it was probably an overreaction to losing all of these things.

"You're with a large partner, Callaway, PGA Tour, you can't do those things now," Mahan later continued. "I think they may have still lived in their small ecosystem and didn't realize they had entered a large ecosystem, which is awesome through all the hard work you've done, but there are going to be consequences for that. Probably too severe, but that's sort of the world we live in."

Hunter Mahan of the United States hits his shot on the second tee during the first round of the Sony Open in Hawaii at the Waialae Country Club on Jan. 14, 2021, in Honolulu, Hawaii. (Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)

GOOD GOOD GOLF DOESN'T DESERVE TO BE CANCELED FOR THEIR DUMB AD IN COLLABORATION WITH CALLAWAY

Callaway announced in a statement from CEO Chip Brewer that the "content review process was not comprehensive enough," and they have taken "appropriate internal corrective actions and significantly strengthened our approval procedures to help ensure this does not happen again." The statement also explained that Callaway approved the ad before it was posted.

Garrett Clark warms up on the driving range during the 2025 Tour Championship Creator Classic, prior to TOUR Championship, at East Lake Golf Club, on Aug. 20, 2025, in Atlanta, Georgia. (Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

The company also explained in a later statement that it was committing "$1 million to support organizations working to prevent violence against women, provide resources to survivors, and advance education and awareness efforts."

Hours after Callaway announced that it was ending its relationship with Good Good, the PGA Tour announced that Good Good had pulled out of its sponsorship of the scheduled event in November. The PGA Tour has the now-sponsorless event listed as the Austin Championship on its official website.

articles.title: Ed Miliband promises ‘comprehensive reset’ of UK policy toward Israel
articles.excerpt:
Foreign secretary tells MPs he will try to stop illegal settlements carving up the West Bank

Ed Miliband has promised to “reset” Britain’s policy on Israel, saying he will try to stop British compani...
articles.body_text:
Foreign secretary tells MPs he will try to stop illegal settlements carving up the West Bank

Ed Miliband has promised to “reset” Britain’s policy on Israel, saying he will try to stop British companies helping build settlements in the West Bank.

Speaking to the Commons for the first time as foreign secretary, Miliband said he would set out measures to prevent UK involvement in projects such as the illegal E1 plan, which critics say would split the West Bank in half.

Tuesday’s comments came after Israel issued tenders for around a third of the 3,400 homes planned for the project. Miliband called the settlement “the crossing of a red line”.

He said: “It cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable. This government will not acquiesce in the destruction of the two-state solution. We will act, and I will set out a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks.

“I want a comprehensive reset of our approach on these issues because it is necessary, it is high time.”

Ministers have been under pressure for weeks to place tighter sanctions on Israel, specifically in relation to the E1 plan.

Last month, Israel invited companies to bid for contracts to build 1,200 homes for the project between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Ma’ale Adumim.

A group of former British diplomats called on the government in May to threaten action against any companies bidding to build any illegal settlement “designed to divide the West Bank in two and destroy Palestine’s viability”. They warned that E1 was part of Israel’s “systemic West Bank annexation”.

Other governments have condemned the project. The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz – usually one of Israel’s staunchest defenders – called it a “big mistake”.

The UK joined a group of 20 other countries, including France, Germany and Italy, as well as the European Union, to issue a joint statement calling E1 “unacceptable”.

The statement said: “The E1 settlement will undermine the prospect of the two-state solution by driving a wedge through the West Bank and harming the territorial contiguity of the Palestinian territories.”

Miliband said: “We need to look, and we are looking indeed, at our wider economic relationship with the occupied territories and the different tools we have to tackle it.

“I want to be very clear: we do not want British companies financing, constructing, or advertising new settlements. The work we are now undertaking is how we can stop that. And as I say, I’ll have more to say soon.”

Ministers are under pressure to go further and ban trade in goods and services with people or organisations linked to illegal settlements.

James Naish, the Labour MP for Rushcliffe in Nottinghamshire, said: “Does the foreign secretary accept that this pace of expansion shows that current UK measures are failing to change Israeli government behaviour, and that a trade ban is now the necessary next step?”

Stephen Doughty, a Foreign Office minister, indicated this could be included in the government’s measures. He said: “We have absolutely condemned the settler violence, the settler terrorism that we have seen, absolutely our condemnation of the proposals for E1 and all illegal settlements, and indeed we have joined other countries around the world in condemning this proposal and been very, very clear with the government of Israel that this must stop.

“The prime minister has been very clear that we need to do more, including looking at further sanctions, both those involved in the violence in Gaza, but also looking at measures to ban trade in goods with illegal settlements.”

The Israeli embassy to London responded by referring to previous comments by Gideon Sa’ar, Israel’s foreign minister, who said: “If Britain acts against the state of Israel, the state of Israel will act against Britain. We have the tools. The period is over when people act against the state of Israel and the state of Israel doesn’t respond.”

articles.title: House passes funding bill to avoid shutdown before midterms
articles.excerpt:
Continuing resolution to approve government spending until 11 December passes 370-48 and will now go to Trump

The US House of Representatives on Tuesday approved legislation to prevent a government s...
articles.body_text:
Continuing resolution to approve government spending until 11 December passes 370-48 and will now go to Trump

The US House of Representatives on Tuesday approved legislation to prevent a government shutdown through the midterms, as both parties opted to defuse a volatile dispute ahead of the November elections that will decide the balance of power in Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

A continuing resolution (CR) authorizing government spending until 11 December passed the House by a 370-48 vote, with only 19 Republicans and 29 Democrats in opposition. Had it not passed, lawmakers would have had until the end of September to approve new funding or face a government shutdown.

The measure, which keeps federal spending at their current levels until the CR expires, now heads to Trump’s desk, after the Senate approved it last month by an overwhelming margin.

In July, the House passed its own CR that would have authorized government spending until 4 December, but most Democrats rejected it for funding immigration enforcement agencies without including new guardrails on their conduct that they had demanded, and the Senate never took it up.

The relatively uneventful end to the annual government funding debate comes as lawmakers step up their campaigning ahead of the 3 November elections, in which most forecasters believe Democratic candidates have an edge in retaking the majority in the House of Representatives.

There are mounting signs that the minority may also be able to regain control of the Senate by winning seats in at least three states that voted for Trump two years ago, as the president struggles with approval ratings driven lower by persistent inflation and the war with Iran.

In the run-up to the vote, top House Democrats said they were ready to support the Senate measure, noting it included policy tweaks that the party supported. Among those was a delay until 11 December on a new rule by the White House office of management and budget that Democrats feared would allow the Trump administration to cancel grants at any time for any reason.

“Given that the objectives that we had were met, I think that there’s going to be broad bipartisan support,” Pete Aguilar, the Democratic caucus chair, told reporters ahead of the vote.

After losing control of both houses of Congress in the 2024 elections, Democrats repeatedly used the Senate’s filibuster to force the government closed and push the Republican majority into compromising over their preferred policies.

Last year, Senate Democrats instigated a government shutdown by refusing to vote for any spending bill that did not extend subsidies for Affordable Care Act health plans.

That led to the longest funding lapse in US history, but ultimately no agreement to keep the cost offsets going after the shutdown ended 43 days later.

Some government agencies shut down again briefly earlier this year after Democrats held up a funding bill for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in protest of the killings by federal agents of two US citizens in Minneapolis during an intensive immigration enforcement drive.

While an agreement was reached to resolve that blockade, the two parties did not agree on funding the DHS for weeks, as Democrats held out for reforms to immigration enforcement operations.

A bipartisan agreement was reached to fund the department operations exclusive of the agencies involved in Trump’s mass deportation push, then Republicans passed a party-line bill that allocated funding to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection for the duration of Trump’s presidency, with no reforms to immigration enforcement.

articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

FIRST ON FOX: Dozens of suspected migrants were rescued from a 30-foot pleasure craft after spending two days stranded without fuel, food or water, nearly 90 miles off the Southern California coast, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.

The Coast Guard said 37 suspected migrants were aboard the boat when crews reached it Friday, about 88 miles from Channel Islands Harbor.

The rescue began around 3:40 p.m., when the boat’s operator radioed the Coast Guard for help.

OVERCROWDED MIGRANT VESSEL WITH 240 PEOPLE ON BOARD INTERCEPTED NEAR TURKS AND CAICOS

The Coast Guard brought the suspected migrant group ashore and turned them over to U.S. Border Patrol personnel. (U.S. Coast Guard)

The operator said the boat had been drifting for two days without fuel, food or water and had no personal safety equipment.

The suspected migrants were adrift without fuel, food or water for two days, the Coast Guard said. (U.S. Coast Guard)

The Coast Guard sent several crews to the area, including the cutters Sockeye and Halibut, boats from stations in Los Angeles-Long Beach and Channel Islands, and an air crew.

Crews found the boat around 8:30 p.m. and brought all 37 suspected migrants aboard the Sockeye.

The 37 suspected migrants were rescued from a 30-foot pleasure craft about 90 miles off Southern California's coast, the Coast Guard said. (U.S. Coast Guard)

"I could not be prouder of the Coast Guard crews on scene who were directly responsible for 37 lives saved last night," said Master Chief Peter Nelson, the Sockeye’s officer in charge.

COAST GUARD SEIZES 7K POUNDS OF COCAINE WORTH MORE THAN $54 MILLION NEAR PUERTO RICO, FIVE ARRESTED

The Coast Guard brought all 37 suspected migrants to Coast Guard Base Los Angeles-Long Beach, where they were turned over to U.S. Border Patrol. (U.S. Coast Guard)

Nelson said crews carried out the rescue at night in rough conditions far from shore.

"Despite operating far offshore in rough conditions at night, they persevered until every person in danger was rescued," Nelson said. "Their extraordinary professionalism, superb judgment, and impeccable seamanship shined throughout the entire case."

The Sockeye brought the group to Coast Guard Base Los Angeles-Long Beach, where they were turned over to U.S. Border Patrol.

The Coast Guard did not say where the group was from, where the boat began its journey or where it was headed. (U.S. Coast Guard)

The Coast Guard did not immediately say where the group was from, where the boat began its journey or where it was headed.

articles.title: Week one upset special: These three college football teams should be on upset alert this weekend
articles.excerpt:
Will LSU be able to start former NFL players??

I hope you all canceled your plans for the next 20 or so Saturdays, because college football is back.

After a nice appetizer over the weekend courtesy ...
articles.body_text:
Will LSU be able to start former NFL players??

I hope you all canceled your plans for the next 20 or so Saturdays, because college football is back.

After a nice appetizer over the weekend courtesy of week zero, the action ramps up in earnest with a full slate of games going all the way through Labor Day.

There are quite a few high-profile match ups on the docket for week one, and with that comes the inevitability of upsets.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

It is college football, after all, and no season opener would be complete without a few shockers (happy 19th anniversary to Appalachian State's win at The Big House, by the way).

With that in mind, here are three teams favored to win this weekend that should be on upset alert.

A view of an Auburn Tigers helmet sitting on a bench at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas on Nov. 7, 2015. (Bob Levey/Getty Images)

Let me preface this pick by saying that I truly believe Auburn head coach Alex Golesh will do great things on The Plains, but this game reeks of upset potential.

The Tigers are breaking in a ton of new players as well as the aforementioned new coaching staff, and the fact that this is at a neutral site in Atlanta makes this game extra wonky.

The Baylor Bears weren't exactly world beaters last year, and new quarterback DJ Lagway was a train wreck at Florida in 2025, but he was dealing with a litany of injuries all last season as well as having to perform in a Billy Napier offense, so I expect the junior signal caller to look more like a five-star than he did throughout much of his time in Gainesville.

SLEEPER TEAMS FROM EACH POWER 4 CONFERENCE: WHO WILL EXCEED EXPECTATIONS THIS COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON?

Auburn won this game handily last year, too, but did so with an entirely different coaching staff and set of players, so that result is a largely irrelevant data point.

I wouldn't put money on the Bears to win this game outright, but I wouldn't be shocked if they did, and I almost expect them to get inside that 7.5 number as Golesh tries to work through some first-game jitters.

UNLV Rebels running back Keyvone Lee (2) runs into tight end Matt Byrnes (85) after the handoff against the Ohio Bobcats during the second half at the Ford Center at The Star in Frisco, Texas, on Dec. 23, 2025. (Raymond Carlin III/Imagn Images)

If you had asked me to pick this game seven days ago, I would have hammered UNLV, but with the benefit of seeing both teams perform during week zero, I might have to pivot to the Rainbow Warriors of Hawaii.

The Rebels struggled to stop Memphis's offense in the 27-21 loss to the Tigers at home, and I have a feeling some of that defensive fog lingers for this game too.

Conversely, Hawaii might have actually gained some confidence in their week zero loss to Stanford, a game in which they were the underdogs and were leading midway through the fourth quarter.

The biggest factor here is that the game is in Honolulu, and that kind of trans-Pacific travel coupled with a season-opening loss could spell trouble for the Rebels.

If that does happen, and UNLV goes from G6 Playoff darlings to 0-2, some uncomfortable conversations will start to spring up about head coach Dan Mullen's future in Vegas.

And no number of Elvis impersonators will be able to save him from that.

LSU Tigers CB Mansoor Delane celebrates a defensive stop against the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium in S.C. (Ken Ruinard/USA TODAY Network)

A good old-fashioned Tiger on Tiger match up, and this one has some layers to it, so bare with me.

When these two teams met last year in South Carolina, it was thought to be somewhat of a College Football Playoff preview, with both LSU and Clemson ranked in the top-ten to start the season.

As it turned out, both teams wound up winning only seven games apiece and LSU even sent head coach Brian Kelly packing.

Now, the Bayou Bengals have Lane Kiffin roaming their sidelines armed with a $40 million roster, but there have been several distractions to come out of Baton Rouge in recent weeks, most notably the staff being at the center of the controversy regarding NFL players going back to college.

That could prove to be enough of a headache for the coaches and players to make what should have been a fairly comfortable win into a dog fight, but that's not to say Clemson can't win this game even on their own merits.

The talent disparity between the two teams isn't as wide as some say it is, and Clemson has some serious firepower at the wide receiver position as well as along its front seven.

I do worry about how Clemson starting quarterback Christopher Vizzina will handle the noise in Death Valley with this being only his second career start, but he has the talent profile as well as the aforementioned stable of receivers to get the job done.

LSU can ill afford to overlook this game, even as double-digit favorites, and no one should be shocked if Clemson comes in and plants their flag in Tiger Stadium.

articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A hiker who fell 20 feet in a North Carolina gorge and sustained serious injuries was airlifted out of harm’s way over the weekend.

Emergency crews were called around 2 p.m. Sunday amid reports of a fallen climber along a steep section of Shortoff Mountain in Linville Gorge.

"The lead climber was attempting to place gear approximately 40 feet above the ledge when they took a lead fall of approximately 15–20 feet," Burke Rescue Inc. and SAR posted on its Facebook page, "during which they swung away from the climbing wall and struck an adjacent rock pillar."

An online fundraiser shared by Burke Rescue identified the climber as Jacob Gregory.

HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF

Emergency crews airlifted a climber who fell over the weekend while climbing Linville Gorge in North Carolina. (Burke Rescue Inc and SAR)

Paramedics initially responded, rappelled down to the climber, and assessed the patient while additional resources were requested.

"After a request for whole blood, a Burke Rescue volunteer ran approximately 1.5 miles, covering 1,000 feet of elevation in just 31 minutes," the Facebook post states, "while carrying critical whole blood to the patient to help stabilize them for transport."

AMERICAN RED CROSS DECLARES NATIONAL BLOOD CRISIS AS TYPE O SUPPLY DROPS TO DANGEROUS LEVELS

Emergency crews seen during an airlift rescue in North Carolina of a climber who fell while hiking. (Burke Rescue Inc and SAR)

A North Carolina Helo-Aquatic Rescue Team Black Hawk helicopter was eventually called to assist with an air rescue because of the steep, rugged terrain.

The helicopter, known as "Kill Devil 244," lifted the climber off the mountain and took him to Charlotte for medical treatment. The rescue involved two dozen agencies from surrounding counties.

RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION

"It took an extraordinary number of people, coordination, and courage to get Jacob from that remote mountainside to the care he needed," the online fundraiser said. "To every responder who answered that call: thank you. You saved a life and brought a husband, father, brother, son, friend and loved one to safety."

A climber was airlifted to safety on Sunday and falling 20 feet while on a mountain. (Burke Rescue Inc and SAR)

Burke Rescue noted that climbing comes with inherent risks and urged climbers to "know your abilities" as well as use appropriate equipment.

articles.title: Two Democrats rescue Mike Johnson's anti-socialism resolution in stunning move
articles.excerpt:
House GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain spoke with Fox News Digital about the fight against socialists and a pair of votes in Congress to test House Democrats' resolve.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-L...
articles.body_text:
House GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain spoke with Fox News Digital about the fight against socialists and a pair of votes in Congress to test House Democrats' resolve.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., scored a commanding victory on Tuesday after overcoming a House GOP rebellion to advance a resolution to condemn socialism.

House conservatives had threatened to tank a procedural vote, called a "rule vote," meant to unlock debate on several bills GOP leaders wanted lawmakers to vote on this week.

But the rebels' issue was not with the measure itself, nor the bills it would have allowed the House to pass. Their votes were a protest against how their leaders handled a plan to avert a government shutdown just before the midterm elections, a short-term funding bill called a continuing resolution (CR).

JOHNSON SCORES WIN AS CONSERVATIVE REBELS END HOUSE FLOOR BLOCKADE OVER VOTER ID BILL

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., speaks to reporters outside the House chambers in the U.S. Capitol Building in Washington, D.C., on June 30, 2026. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"NO ON CR. NO ON RULE THAT DOES NOT ALLOW US TO AMEND AND FIX THE CR: The House of Representatives will be voting for a government funding continuing resolution TODAY that FAILS to deliver on common-sense policies for the American people," Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, wrote on X.

House Freedom Caucus Chair Andy Harris, R-Md., also told reporters he would vote against the rule in protest of the CR.

A handful of GOP lawmakers took issue with how the Senate modified an original House-passed CR, including adding an unrelated measure to delay a congressionally approved hemp product ban by 30 days and a provision curbing the Trump administration’s control over federal grants.

TENSIONS ERUPT IN HOUSE HEARING AS GOP ADVANCES ANTI-SOCIALISM RESOLUTION WHILE DEMS RAGE: 'SILLY SEASON'

"The Senate did violence to our bill," Rep. Keith Self, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital. "Hemp and the grants are the two big ones…and frankly, I just don’t think CRs ought to be on suspension…when you put it on suspension, you’re not asking for my vote, okay, you’re going to get Democrats."

Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, speaks about the ongoing negotiations between House leadership, the White House and the House Freedom Caucus on the "One, Big, Beautiful Bill" at the U.S. Capitol Building on May 21, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

Roy also criticized the bill for not cutting off funding to sanctuary jurisdictions or abortion providers like Planned Parenthood.

DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

Voting on a bill under "suspension" means it gets fast-tracked past multiple procedural hurdles in exchange for raising the threshold for passage from a simple majority to two-thirds. That means the rule vote's survival does not affect whether the CR passes or fails.

A CR is a short-term extension of current federal funding levels. It's normally used to give lawmakers extra time to cobble together a new budget for the next fiscal year, which begins Oct. 1.

Workers begin construction of a large metal fence alongside construction supplies on the east side of the U.S. Capitol Building on Aug. 25, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images)

The CR up for a vote on Tuesday would kick the government shutdown fight to a Dec. 11 deadline.

A rule vote traditionally falls along party lines and until recently, it was unheard of for lawmakers to defy their leaders by joining the other side to defeat it. But it's become increasingly common in recent years for lawmakers, specifically on the right, to weaponize it as a form of protest.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

articles.title: Health crisis looming as Gaza heads towards rainy season, warns WHO
articles.excerpt:
The approach of winter and cold rains are set to worsen a public health crisis that already has a firm grip in the embattled Gaza Strip, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

Recent water t...
articles.body_text:
The approach of winter and cold rains are set to worsen a public health crisis that already has a firm grip in the embattled Gaza Strip, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

Recent water testing has shown there is a clear deterioration in the quality of water in the Palestinian enclave and diarrhea cases have surged, the United Nations health agency said on Tuesday, noting that the approach of winter threatens to exasperate the situation.

Much of Gaza has been destroyed during Israel’s genocidal war, and it remains under blockade, leaving much of its population without sufficient shelter and exposed to a lack of functioning infrastructure.

“Whilst we fail to provide people with the minimum quantities of water, water quality and water contamination remains a major issue,” said Reinhilde Van de Weerdt, the WHO’s representative in the Palestinian territories.

Potential flooding resulting from winter rains “will [send] the sewage, the waste and contaminated water into the pl000aces where people sleep, cook and care for their loved ones,” she warned.

Testing of approximately 6,700 water samples over the first eight months of 2026 indicated that “microbiological contamination almost tripled,” she told reporters in Geneva, speaking from Gaza.

Contamination increased from under six percent in January to over 18 percent in August, the tests showed.

Cases of acute diarrhea have almost doubled since March, jumping from around 27,000 cases to over 48,000, Van de Weerdt noted.

However, the WHO official insisted there is still time to prevent a public health disaster. She called for “unimpeded and expedited entry of humanitarian supplies”.

Materials needed for permanent shelter and sustainable provision of water and waste management are vital, she said. More laboratory supplies are urgently needed to help confirm the causes of disease and better respond to outbreaks.

Israel has been using water access as a “weapon” in Gaza, Doctors Without Borders declared in April. The group pointed to data from the United Nations, European Union and World Bank indicating that Israel had destroyed or damaged nearly 90 percent of water and sanitation infrastructure in the territory.

articles.title: Vanuatu pushes France to accept ICJ jurisdiction in Pacific islands dispute
articles.excerpt:
The Pacific island nation of Vanuatu has filed an application with the International Court of Justice (ICJ) seeking sovereignty over two small Pacific islands controlled by France.

The Hague-based co...
articles.body_text:
The Pacific island nation of Vanuatu has filed an application with the International Court of Justice (ICJ) seeking sovereignty over two small Pacific islands controlled by France.

The Hague-based court said in a statement on Tuesday that Vanuatu’s application concerns sovereignty over Umaenupne, also known as Matthew Island, and Umaeneg/Leka, or Hunter Island.

The case seeks closure on a decades-old territorial dispute rooted in the region’s colonial history. Far-right parties in France are seeking to use the case as a political weapon.

The ICJ, also known as the World Court, will not immediately take up the case because France has not accepted the court’s compulsory jurisdiction over disputes with other states.

Vanuatu’s application has been sent to Paris to determine whether France agrees to let the court hear the case.

“No action will be taken in the proceedings unless and until France consents to the Court’s jurisdiction in the case,” the ICJ said.

The dispute has become part of a wider debate over France’s colonial legacy in the Pacific.

Vanuatu, jointly ruled by France and Britain until independence in 1980, argues that its decolonisation will not be complete until the islands are returned under its control.

The issue has also been seized upon by France’s far right, which has accused President Emmanuel Macron’s government of being prepared to surrender French territory, a claim Paris has repeatedly rejected.

Vanuatu has challenged French sovereignty over the islands since gaining independence, arguing that the colonial-era arrangement placing them under French control was made without consulting the Indigenous population.

Matthew and Hunter are uninhabited volcanic islands in the South Pacific, about 300 kilometres (190 miles) east of the French territory of New Caledonia and southeast of Vanuatu.

While the islands themselves are small, sovereignty affects control over surrounding waters, including fishing rights and access to seabed resources.

In 2025, France and Vanuatu agreed to new rounds of bilateral negotiations over the islands and their maritime boundaries after earlier talks in 2018 and 2019.

Earlier this year, Vanuatu said negotiations had reached an impasse and that it would take the dispute to an international court.

The ICJ, the United Nations’ highest court, deals with disputes between states and frequently rules on disagreements over land and maritime boundaries.

articles.title: Baby killed after illegal immigrant allegedly strikes family at grocery store parking lot
articles.excerpt: ICE arrested Giovana Mercedes Moreno Ochompy, a former Illinois high school teacher and illegal immigrant, in connection with a triple murder involving the Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang. Chicago poli...
articles.body_text:
ICE arrested Giovana Mercedes Moreno Ochompy, a former Illinois high school teacher and illegal immigrant, in connection with a triple murder involving the Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang. Chicago police initially released her due to sanctuary city policies, without notifying ICE. Tom Homan, former acting ICE director, criticizes these policies, arguing they hinder federal law enforcement and endanger public safety.

An illegal immigrant from Guatemala was charged with manslaughter after allegedly crashing into a mother and her two children, killing her 9-month-old son, in a New Jersey grocery store parking lot Friday, according to authorities.

A 9-month-old boy was pronounced dead at Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune after Maria Cobon-Guzman allegedly struck his mother and the baby carriage carrying him and his 5-year-old sister in the parking lot of a kosher grocery store in Jackson on Friday.

"An innocent baby would still be alive today had it not been for Joe Biden’s disastrous open border and reckless immigration policy that released countless illegal aliens into our country," a DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS ANNOUNCES NEW JERSEY ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ARRESTS AS NEWARK PROTESTS RAGE OUTSIDE FACILITY

Gov. Mikie Sherrill, left; Maria Cobon-Guzman, inset (Jim Watson/Getty Images; Ocean County Sheriff's Office)

"We are urging the Ocean County Jail to honor ICE’s detainers on these two criminal illegal aliens to take them out of American communities once and for all," the spokesperson said of the Republican-friendly county in the otherwise blue state.

All three victims were transported to Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune. The mother and her five-year-old child remained hospitalized in stable condition, while the 9-month-old boy died.

Another woman, Ariadna Lazaro-Flores, was also charged in the incident after she reportedly allowed Cobon-Guzman to drive her car knowing she was unlicensed. An inmate report listed Lazaro-Flores as charged with "endangering the welfare of an incompetent person."

Both women illegally entered the U.S. during the Biden administration, with Lazaro-Flores doing so five times in October 2023 and being removed each time, DHS told Fox News Digital.

"She last illegally entered the United States through the Biden Administration’s open border at an unknown place and time," the agency said.

ICE MAKES NATIONWIDE ARRESTS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, MURDERERS, PEDOPHILES IN HOLIDAY BLITZ

Cobon-Guzman entered once but was released unvetted into the nation’s interior, DHS added. On July 31, an immigration judge issued an order of removal against her.

"New Jersey must honor ICE's detainers on these two criminal illegal aliens to take them out of American communities once and for all,"," the agency tweeted.

Democratic New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, who signed legislation codifying New Jersey’s Immigrant Trust Directive, had not commented as of Tuesday morning.

When reached for comment, a Sherrill spokesman directed Fox News Digital to Attorney General Jennifer Davenport. Davenport did not immediately respond.

Observers took notice of the relative silence as Sherrill's social media posts about other things including a critique of President Donald Trump's battle with Iran sparked outrage:

"How about sticking to doing something about the highest property taxes in the US [or] stopping illegals from killing and maiming us?" read one response.

The Trust Directive, as drafted by Davenport predecessor Gurbir Grewal, limits voluntary assistance New Jersey law enforcement may provide DHS.

New Jersey Republicans fired back at Trenton leadership, suggesting they created the conditions to allow the tragedy to occur.

"An innocent baby is dead. A mother and another child were seriously injured. Now, ICE is seeking custody of the two women charged in connection with the crash," the state party said in a statement.

"This should not be complicated: New Jersey must comply with ICE detainers. Governor Sherrill has a responsibility to put the safety of New Jersey families ahead of sanctuary policies. When federal immigration authorities seek custody of individuals charged with serious crimes, the state should cooperate — not stand in the way."

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

articles.title: Sarah Ferguson plots bold return to Britain after Epstein scandal shattered reputation: expert

articles.body_text:
Andrew Lownie, author of "Entitled," weighs in on former Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson’s evolving relationship amid royal scrutiny. The exes were once known as the "happiest divorced couple."

Sarah Ferguson has made a career out of comebacks — and after seven months largely hidden from public view, the former Duchess of York may be preparing for another.

Ferguson, 66, may be ready to step back into the spotlight, with one royal commentator describing the former Duchess of York as a "chameleon" who has repeatedly managed to reinvent herself.

"Sarah Ferguson is forever the chameleon," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "She always seems to bounce back."

SARAH FERGUSON IS HOPING 'TO EVAPORATE LIKE MIST' AS SHE'S SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 7 MONTHS: EXPERT

Sarah Ferguson is reportedly preparing to return to public life after spending seven months largely out of the spotlight. (Rob Kim/Getty Images for Global Citizen)

"The one person who believes in Sarah is Sarah!" Chard added.

One element of Ferguson's reported fresh start could be a new home in Britain. Chard said she understands Ferguson will be based in the Home Counties in a "£10,000 a month plush gated property with granny annex."

But a new residence may only be part of the attempted reset.

Chard said Ferguson has attracted interest from television producers and could use a documentary or interview to put forward her version of events.

"Sarah has admittedly made some silly decisions. However, it's reported that she is lined up to appear in a TV documentary when settled in Britain," Chard said. "This is one of the options to put her side of the story forward, essentially a ‘Tell All’ interview. She has been bombarded with TV production offers. However, she is considering working on her own programme to retain control."

FORMER PRINCE ANDREW FACES WIDENING MISCONDUCT PROBE AS POLICE LAUNCH WITNESS HUNT

Sarah Ferguson is said to be planning a fresh start in Britain while considering television opportunities that could allow Sarah Ferguson to tell her side of the story. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

After Andrew lost his royal titles in October 2025 and was forced to vacate Royal Lodge, Ferguson also had to find somewhere else to live. The former Duchess of York has reportedly been spending her time abroad. Ferguson had been staying at a chalet in the Austrian Alps, People reported.

The release of millions of DOJ documents in late January brought renewed attention to Ferguson's relationship with Epstein, including emails seemingly showing she remained friendly with him after his conviction. The fallout cost Ferguson charity affiliations, contributed to the closure of Sarah's Trust and damaged several of her business ventures.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Helena Chard described Sarah Ferguson as "forever the chameleon" and said she has been "plotting her way back." (Hollie Adams/WPA Pool/Getty Images)

Ferguson’s time away from the U.K. also coincided with mounting turmoil surrounding her ex-husband, the forme Prince Andrew, who was arrested in February amid the investigation into his ties to Epstein.

One subject Ferguson reportedly does not want at the center of her new narrative is Andrew.

"There is no mention of Andrew Mountbatten Windsor for now," Chard said. "Her priority is telling her story and the very mention of Andrew's name is a hindrance."

Separating Ferguson's future from the controversies of her past may prove difficult – royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams offered a harsher assessment of Ferguson's record, calling her "a disaster as an entitled and shameless member of the royal family."

Richard Fitzwilliams argued that Sarah Ferguson’s history of controversies could make another comeback difficult despite her ability to recover from past scandals. (Mark Cuthbert/UK Press via Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"When she was a working royal she was a catastrophe from the start," Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital.

He pointed to Ferguson's "seemingly endless debts," the infamous "toe sucking" episode and the "fake sheikh disaster" as examples of controversies she managed to survive.

"Somehow she bounced back from each setback," Fitzwilliams said.

That ability to recover eventually culminated in a remarkable return to the royal fold. But Fitzwilliams believes Ferguson's latest controversy has placed her in a substantially more difficult position.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Richard Fitzwilliams also questioned whether the public would believe Sarah Ferguson if the former Duchess of York moved forward with plans to tell her story. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"The groveling, often farcical emails she sent to the deceased paedophile Jeffrey Epstein have finally landed her in disgrace, and she has been out of the public gaze for seven months," he said.

For Ferguson, who Chard says "always seems to bounce back," the next chapter could therefore become a test of whether her well-established ability to reinvent herself still works.

"Whether anyone believes a word she says is another matter," he said.
