Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports.

articles.title: Kyle Busch's final words about Daytona come with a sobering Dale Earnhardt twist
articles.excerpt: Fellow driver Ricky Stenhouse Jr. pays tribute to NASCAR legend Kyle Busch after his sudden passing, reflecting on his competitive spirit and dedication to racing. Stenhouse discusses Busch's impact o...
articles.body_text:
Fellow driver Ricky Stenhouse Jr. pays tribute to NASCAR legend Kyle Busch after his sudden passing, reflecting on his competitive spirit and dedication to racing. Stenhouse discusses Busch's impact on the sport and his family.

It doesn't take long to spot a Kyle Busch fan at Daytona International Speedway.

In fact, drive under the tunnel and into the infield, and a "Rowdy Forever" banner is the first thing that greets you. It's not the only one. Not even close.

They're everywhere this weekend. Of course, that's expected.

This is the first NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona since Busch's stunning death in May. The Coke Zero Sugar 400 is set to close the regular season later tonight — a little over three months since the sport lost its modern day Dale Earnhardt.

For better and for worse, those two will forever be attached at the hip.

KYLE BUSCH'S CHILLING MESSAGE AFTER FINAL NASCAR WIN A PAINFUL ENDING FOR MOURNING FANS

Kyle Busch, driver of the No. 18 M&M's Toyota, stands on the grid during qualifying for the NASCAR Cup Series 62nd Annual Daytona 500 at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Fla., on Feb. 9, 2020. (Getty Images)

Busch's death in May was the first major NASCAR death for an active driver since Earnhardt died on the final turn of the 2001 Daytona 500.

For decades, Daytona gave Dale fits. He could win all the races, except the race.

Busch won just once at Daytona during his two decades in a Cup car, and never won a 500. It was the crown jewel he never got.

Lord knows he tried. Came close a couple times, too. Earlier this year, Busch grabbed his first Daytona 500 pole. He led 19 laps, but he fizzled late.

No, Kyle never loved Daytona the way Dale Earnhardt did. But he appreciated it. He respected it.

Signs for Kyle Busch at Daytona. (Zach Dean/ OutKick)

During February's 500, he led the third lap of the race, which was dedicated to Dale Earnhardt on what was the 25th anniversary of his death.

"Led lap 3 for Dale plus a few more today," he posted days after the race. "Made it to the end, just not in the right spot."

Now, the series returns for the first time since his death — and for the first time without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field since 1978.

Yep. That's right. Saturday night's race will be the first Cup race at Daytona without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field in 48 years. February 19, 1978.

For those who don't remember, Bobby Allison won that Daytona 500. Earnhardt would make his first Daytona start months later in the Firecracker 400.

Incredible. Forty-eight years. Nearly five decades!

Dale Earnhardt checks out the view from the newly completed Earnhardt Grandstand during winter testing at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Fla., two weeks before the Daytona 500. (Getty Images)

So, yes, this sport has Earnhardt and Busch in its blood. Dale died in the '01 Daytona 500, which was Kurt Busch's first race. Kyle came into the series five years later as a rookie with Hendrick Motorsports.

UNEARTHED FAN VIDEO SHOWS WHO KYLE BUSCH REALLY WAS, NASCAR'S DARKEST HOUR & BUBBA WALLACE'S 'ROWDY' STORY

He'd go on to win 63 Cup races over the next two decades, including a pair of championships. He had 234 wins across all three NASCAR national series.

Busch won one Coca-Cola 600, two Southern 500s, and three Indianapolis 500 victories. He won once official race at Daytona, but did win a couple duels and the one Busch Clash on the road course back in 2021.

Kyle Busch, driver of the #8 Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen Chevrolet, waves to fans as he walks onstage during driver introductions before the NASCAR Cup Series Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Fla., on Aug. 24, 2024. (Getty Images)

"Yeah, it’s a box we got to check," he said earlier this year. "Here we are. This is an opportunity to be able to do that. I’ve come down here a lot of years."

Daytona was never great to Kyle. It wasn't his favorite place to race. He didn't have the best luck.

But coming back here this weekend, it's clear this place misses him.

And like Dale, he's still everywhere you look.

articles.title: Russian drone strike on Kyiv warehouse storing weapons kills at least 37
articles.excerpt:
Attack on depot owned by Ukraine military causes detonations and huge fire, damaging residential buildings

At least 37 people have been killed after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near Kyiv’s wes...
articles.body_text:
Attack on depot owned by Ukraine military causes detonations and huge fire, damaging residential buildings

At least 37 people have been killed after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near Kyiv’s western suburbs that was storing “explosive objects”.

The attack damaged at least 50 residential buildings, including a care home for elderly and disabled people, and sparked a huge fire and explosions in the Bucha district of the Kyiv region. The regional governor, Tymur Tkachenko, said a further 42 people, including four children, had been injured in the strike.

More than 370 people have been evacuated from the area and the evacuation process was continuing, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said. In a statement, he said a warehouse in the town of Myla had been struck, “followed by a detonation”.

The warehouse was a depot owned by the Ukrainian military and stored shells, drones and other munitions, he said in a video address. “The first impact was on a place where ammunition was being stored that absolutely should not have been there – a depot of the defence forces. [There was] detonation of shells, mines, other munitions and drones on a significant scale,” Zelenskyy said.

Criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence, he added.

“There are regulations in place; ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas,” the president said.

“As of now, 27 people have been reported killed. One of those killed was the head of the Dmytrivka community, Taras Didych. He was rescuing people,” he added.

Ukrainian prosecutors said they had opened an investigation into the legality of the “storage of explosive objects and materials”.

The Ukrainian prime minister, Serhii Koretskyi, expressed regret that mistakes had not been learned from a previous deadly strike on a munitions depot in Vyshneve, near Kyiv, in July.

An investigation into that incident, in which 22 people were killed and fires tore through nearby homes, revealed serious failings on the part of a state-owned company, which did not comply with regulations on the proximity of residential buildings.

“Unfortunately, we can already see that the terrible tragedy in Vyshneve did not become a lesson,” Koretskyi said. “In the fifth year of a full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes is criminal negligence. And all those guilty, without exception, must be severely punished so that such situations do not happen again.”

In a statement, Russia’s ministry of defence said it had hit a warehouse in Myla storing components and launch boosters for long-range drones. It said it had also attacked the ports of Mykolaiv and Izmail, as well as a logistics centre and warehouse facilities storing parts for Ukraine’s Flamingo cruise missiles in the Kyiv region.

Elsewhere, Russian attacks across Ukraine’s southern Kherson region killed two people and wounded 27 more on Saturday, including a child, a local official said.

articles.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator fined $172,000 for Trump speech bets
articles.excerpt:
Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Gabriel Perez wagered on Kalshi about words president used in speeches

A White House teleprompter operator who left his post amid accusations that he used in...
articles.body_text:
Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Gabriel Perez wagered on Kalshi about words president used in speeches

A White House teleprompter operator who left his post amid accusations that he used inside knowledge to make bets on Donald Trump’s speeches on an online prediction market has been fined $172,000, according to federal regulators.

Gabriel Perez exploited “material, nonpublic information” that he gathered through his work for the president in order to place wagers on the Kalshi platform “for his personal benefit”, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) maintained in a news release on Friday.

The CFTC ordered Perez to both “disgorge the profits he made from his unlawful [conduct]” totaling $107,539.02 and to pay a civil penalty of $65,000, the agency’s news release said. Such amounts represented “a substantial discount”, the CFTC added, attributing that to what the agency called “Perez’s exemplary cooperation” with its investigation into him.

According to the CFTC, from December to February while working as a White House teleprompter operator, Perez made bets on Kalshi tied to words or phrases that Trump might make during his speeches. Perez’s White House role gave him access to those speeches before the president delivered them, and he “misappropriated that information” to profit, breaching “his duty of trust and confidence”, the CFTC asserted.

Perez – beside being fined – “agreed to cease and desist from further violations” of federal laws prohibiting market manipulation and CFTC regulations, the CFTC said. He was also handed a three-year trading ban.

The CFTC issued its news release about Perez on Friday, about a month after the White House said he no longer had his job there. It was unclear whether Perez resigned or was fired.

Yet his departure came after he was reportedly put on unpaid leave amid an investigation into whether he had used his inside knowledge to win more than $100,000 betting on what Trump would say on big occasions, including his State of the Union address in February. The White House press secretary at the time, Karoline Leavitt, had described the reports of insider trading by Perez as “deeply unfortunate and, frankly, a disgrace”.

Perez earned an annual salary of $175,000 for his teleprompter work, according to White House personnel records.

The case centering on Perez was only the latest to illustrate the continued proliferation of online prediction markets, which allow users to place speculative bets on public events and trends. That has evidently incentivized insider trading.

For instance, about four months before Perez’s fine, federal prosecutors indicted US soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke for allegedly making a $400,000 bet on Kalshi rival platform Polymarket about whether Nicolás Maduro would be removed from Venezuela’s presidency. Van Dyke had worked on the operation to remove Maduro and extradite him to the US on drug-trafficking charges, according to prosecutors.

Furthermore, Kalshi in April also announced fines against three political candidates who bet on their own elections, including one who wagered on whether he would run for office before announcing an independent campaign for a US Senate seat in Virginia.

Trump has defended the prediction market industry, to which his family has business ties. He has advocated against individual US states regulating those markets and has argued that the CFTC should instead carry out that function.

In its news release on Perez’s fine, meanwhile, the CFTC made it a point to thank Kalshi for its “assistance … in this matter”.

articles.title: Mladic died a happy man. He won
articles.excerpt: The death of war criminal Ratko Mladic made headlines across the world. “The Butcher of Bosnia dies in The Hague”, the international media announced, seemingly suggesting that justice has been served ...
articles.body_text:
The death of war criminal Ratko Mladic made headlines across the world. “The Butcher of Bosnia dies in The Hague”, the international media announced, seemingly suggesting that justice has been served at least in his case.

Nothing changed on November 22, 2017 when he was sentenced by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) to life in prison for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes committed in Bosnia more than 10 years earlier. Nothing will change now after his death.

Contrary to what some may think, the world will not become a better place now.

I hate writing this sentence, but here it is: Mladic won. He and his ideas won. He must have died happy, watching the world be overtaken by fascism—a world in which genocide has become normalised. It is what he fought for, after all.

In 2017, after Mladic’s verdict was pronounced, I expressed my fear in an op-ed published by Al Jazeera that his ideas had not been defeated, but would instead spread like a drug-resistant bug, adjusting to different circumstances and times.

It is painful to see today that my prediction has come true. It is clearly visible in the Balkans.

In Serbia—a country the European Union is considering accepting as a member — the ruling regime’s survival depends on maintaining an ideology of death and denial.

Decades after the war, no real change has been achieved. The power of President Aleksandar Vucic, a politician seen as an equal by many EU leaders, is cemented by the denial of responsibility for crimes committed in the 1990s in Croatia, Bosnia and Kosovo.

Then there is Bosnia, a country divided by the Dayton Accords that stopped the shooting and created a divided state that struggles to build a present, much less a future. It is a country where over 100,000 people were killed, and then nothing changed; where genocide denial is an official policy in one part of the country, Republika Srpska; where many of the people who took part in committing war crimes still live freely.

And yet, as much as fascism has maintained its grip on our region, there has also been resistance.

“Ratko Mladic, former head of the Army of Republika Srpska and convicted war criminal, sentenced to life for the genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity and war crimes, died. We will not mourn for him. We will not glorify him […] Death does not delete verdicts. It does not delete established facts. And it does not delete responsibility.”

This is part of a public message from Ostra Nula, a small nongovernmental organisation established by young Serbs in Banja Luka, the capital of the Serb-dominated entity of Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They posted it on social media a few hours before politicians and former soldiers who fought under Mladic took to the streets across Republika Srpska to pay their respects to a murderer who ordered the mass killing, torture and rape of people in Bosnia and then spent 30 years denying his crimes.

Ostra Nula was not the sole voice among Bosnian Serbs that rejected the mourning of Mladic. The magazine Buka, the youth group Kvart, and others, also demonstrated their condemnation of Republika Srpska’s official policy of genocide denial and genocidaire celebration.

Pressure and threats have not stopped people of conscience from fighting against denial of crimes committed during the war, for justice and acknowledgement of moral responsibility. They speak up because they know what fascism left without a response can look like.

In Bosnia, we struggle a lot with the issues left behind by the war, but at least there is awareness. I can’t say the same about most of the rest of the world, which still believes that fascism was defeated 80 years ago.

Many do not recognise it when they see it, but the evidence is there: the public denial of the genocide of the Palestinians, the ignorance of crimes committed in Sudan or the DRC, the indifference to migrants and refugees left to die at sea or on dangerous land routes, the suffering of people deprived of access to basic needs – including medicine – by sanctions, the increase in military spending, inflation, deadly border policing, mass surveillance, and ultra-right politicians in parliaments and governments.

This is the world Mladic dreamed of. And he lived to see it.

The question for the world now is: do you really want to live in Mladic’s dream?

Once, more than 35 years ago, I was forced to live in it, in a Bosnia facing a genocide. And it was a nightmare, an unspeakable horror.

We, genocide survivors, have been calling on the world to wake up. Will it listen?

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: Cells for arrested offenders may run out without early prison release, says Labour
articles.excerpt:
Bridget Phillipson says government would not have to consider releasing prisoners early if Tories had created more capacity

Cells to hold newly arrested people could run out without the early prison ...
articles.body_text:
Bridget Phillipson says government would not have to consider releasing prisoners early if Tories had created more capacity

Cells to hold newly arrested people could run out without the early prison release scheme, a government minister has said.

Bridget Phillipson defended the plan to address the prison capacity crisis in England and Wales by releasing thousands of prisoners early, which has been criticised by domestic abuse charities, bereaved families and probation officers among others.

“We have faced some really difficult and unpalatable choices because of the huge crisis that was left behind in the prisons estate,” the women and equalities minister told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Saturday.

She insisted the “most serious offenders” would not be released early under the scheme, details of which would be set out during the week.

“But the reality of what we are confronting is that, if allowed to go unchecked, we could end up in a position where someone who was arrested for very serious offences, for example, offences related to violence against a woman, and we wouldn’t have anywhere to send that individual. That was the full scale of the real crisis we face.”

Andy Burnham has been facing pressure to balance the competing aims of creating space in prisons and avoiding causing further upset to victims of serious crime. Under the scheme, a sentence would not be ended early but the portion of it served in custody would be shortened. The remainder would be served in the community, a principle that already exists in most sentences.

On Friday, families of those affected by homicide called for those convicted of any form of manslaughter to be excluded from the scheme. In a letter to the justice secretary, Alex Norris, they said they felt victims were “being asked to bear the consequences of the prison capacity crisis”.

Signatories included Emma Webber, whose son Barnaby was stabbed to death in Nottingham in 2023 and whose killer, Valdo Calocane, was convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility. Another was Diana Parkes, whose daughter Joanna Simpson was killed by her estranged husband, Robert Brown, in 2010. Brown was also convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility.

Phillipson said she had the “utmost respect and sympathy for the victims and their families” and blamed the previous Conservative government for allowing the prison capacity problem to fester. “We didn’t create enough prison capacity in the years that they were in government so that we don’t have to be even considering these kinds of options, which – in an ideal world – we would not be having to consider.”

In January, the government announced a set of measures, which came into force in March, that were designed to stave off a looming crisis this summer. Sources indicated, however, that these measures were never thought to be enough to avert further crises. They pointed to the Sentencing Act, which introduces wholesale changes to sentencing, as the government’s plan to fix the issue once and for all.

articles.title: WWE NXT Heatwave 2026 match card, preview and predictions
articles.excerpt:
WWE Hall of Famer Booker T talks to Fox News Digital about the ceiling for rising prospects Kendal Grey and Kali Armstrong.

WWE NXT Heatwave will cap a wild day of professional wrestling on Sunday.

...
articles.body_text:
WWE Hall of Famer Booker T talks to Fox News Digital about the ceiling for rising prospects Kendal Grey and Kali Armstrong.

WWE NXT Heatwave will cap a wild day of professional wrestling on Sunday.

Four championship matches and a submission match will be featured on the card as Heatwave takes place at the Bert Ogden Arena in Edinburg, Texas.

The event marks the first singles match for newcomer Zilla Fatu, who burst onto the NXT scene earlier this month. Fatu immediately went after NXT champion Tony D’Angelo and was thrust into a fatal four-way match with the title on the line.

It’s one of the marquee matches on the card. Read below for the full card, a preview and predictions.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

Jaida Parker speaks to Nattie during NXT at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla., on Aug. 25, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

It’s a rising star versus a legend. Nattie challenged Jaida Parker to a submission match for Heatwave as their rivalry turned up a notch. Parker will have a chance to prove to Nattie and the rest of the WWE Universe that she is who she says she is. Nattie gets a chance to continue to show why she’s the "lowkey legend" who continuously changes the game in the sport.

Prediction: Parker pulls out all the stops.

Tavion Heights and Myles Borne embrace during NXT at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla., on Aug. 4, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

It’s going to be a long night for Myles Borne as he deals with the Vanity Project. First, he teams up with Tavion Heights to go up against Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes. Borne and Heights have only held the tag titles for three weeks after winning it against Baylor and Smokes earlier this month.

Prediction: Borne and Heights hang on to win the tag titles.

Brad Baylor, Jackson Drake and Myka Lockwood of the Vanity Project make their entrance during NXT at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla., on June 30, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

It won’t be long before Borne is in another match with another Vanity Project member. Jackson Drake is looking for his shot at NXT gold in this North American Championship match. Drake beat Shiloh Hill with the help of Naraku to earn the chance at the title. Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes may be unable to take down Borne, but it could end up being Drake’s night.

Prediction: Jackson Drake captures the title

Zaria and Kali Armstrong face off during NXT at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla., on Aug. 25, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

NXT is unifying the Women’s North American Championship and the WWE Women’s Speed Championship. But there’s one wildcard – Kali Armstrong. The former Evolve women’s champion gets her first shot at gold. It will be an uphill battle as Zaria is a worthy champion and Sinclair has proven much in the ring over the last year. Will two reigns come to an end?

Prediction: Kali Armstrong has herself a night

Kiana James faces Kendal Grey during NXT at the WWE Performance Center on June 9, 2026, in Orlando, Fla. (WWE via Getty Images)

Kendal Grey and Kelani Jordan could both be on the main roster right now and be able to swim with the sharks. For now, the NXT Women’s Championship is on the line as Grey goes up against Jordan. Grey has a rocket strapped to her back since she came over from Evolve. Jordan has complained about not getting proper opportunities in NXT as of late. Jordan has a slight advantage since Grey is coming into the match with an ear injury. Jordan is smart enough to use that to her advantage in this one.

Prediction: Grey wins this one in a hard-fought battle.

Zilla Fatu looks on during NXT at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla., on Aug. 25, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

Old NXT, new NXT, a newcomer, an old face – it doesn’t matter. Tony D’Angelo has knocked everyone down since he returned to NXT programming. He now leads the men’s division as the champion but has a huge task in front of him. Grayson Waller is as hungry as ever. Cruz Montana has momentum on his side. Zilla Fatu is looking to make history. D’Angelo has held the NXT Championship for nearly 150 days. He’s the longest reigning champion since Oba Femi in 2025. Could WWE fans see an upset to end Heatwave?

Prediction: Zilla Fatu wins the title in his first singles match on NXT.

WWE NXT Heatwave begins at 3 p.m. ET and can be seen on the CW Network in the United States.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: AEW All In 2026 match card, preview and predictions
articles.excerpt:
All Elite Wrestling and Ring of Honor star Lee Moriarty talks to OutKick about All In 2026.

All Elite Wrestling (AEW) will hold its biggest event of the year at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday.

...
articles.body_text:
All Elite Wrestling and Ring of Honor star Lee Moriarty talks to OutKick about All In 2026.

All Elite Wrestling (AEW) will hold its biggest event of the year at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday.

All In has proven to be a showcase of some of the pro wrestling’s best. This year will be no different with championship matches up and down the card, including the AEW World Championship being on the line between Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay.

All In has also featured some surprises in the past with massive returns and debuts that have shaped the AEW roster.

Read below for a list of the match card, a preview and predictions for how All In will shake out.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

"Hangman" Adam Page wraps barbed wire around his first at AEW Revolution on March 15, 2026. (All Elite Wrestling)

A major trios match will kick off the two-hour All In Buy In and bleed into the first few minutes of All In. Adam Page and Brodido, the Bang Bang Gang, The Conglomeration, the Death Riders, The Demand and The Dogs will compete for the AEW World Trios Championship. But there is a wildcard entrant in this match. It could be anyone or it could be who we’re all expecting it to be. All In has been full of surprises in recent years. Let’s get another one in to start the show off with a bang.

Prediction: Adam Page and Brodido retain the trios title despite the chaos that will ensue.

Kyle Fletcher during AEW Double or Nothing in Queens, N.Y., on May 24, 2026. (Lee South/AEW)

Kyle Fletcher, Konosuke Takeshita and Kazuchika Okada may be three of the best professional wrestlers in the world. Their rivalry began after Takeshita defeated Okada for the AEW International Championship at Double or Nothing. Fletcher returned and turned on Takeshita. Weeks later, Fletcher won the title at Dynamite: Spring Breakin’ and turned the title picture on its head. Now, the three men will meet at All In. And while it may seem like Fletcher and Okada are on the same page, with the title on the line, it’ll be every man for himself.

Prediction: Kyle Fletcher, somehow, pulls it out and retains the title.

Kevin Knight competes inside the ring during New Japan Pro-Wrestling at Korakuen Hall in Tokyo on May 15, 2025. (Etsuo Hara/Getty Images)

Kevin Knight has been the TNT champion for more than 135 days after winning a 10-man Casino Gauntlet match in Vancouver back in April. He’s gone from a fan favorite to the most hated after he turned on "Speedball" Mike Bailey and aligned himself, loosely, with the Don Callis Family. He’s been one of the top stars on the AEW roster since then but may have feuded with the wrong guy in Darby Allin. The challenger has proven that he’s willing to go above and beyond to win any match – even without gold on the line. Allin has been back in the fray for some gold since losing his AEW world title at Double or Nothing to MJF. As he’s dealt with Knight’s mind games, Allin has still shown he’s not willing to go down easy. This will be a big matchup.

Prediction: Darby Allin ends Knight’s title reign.

Megan Bayne enters the ring during the women's pro-wrestling event Stardom at Korakuen Hall in Tokyo on Nov. 7, 2025. (Etsuo Hara/Getty Images)

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, the Divine Dominion have been at the top of the AEW women’s tag team division since March and have dispatched every opponent who have come their way. The Brawling Birds, Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter, have been two women who have not backed down from challenging Bayne and Kross. The Brawling Birds have their home country behind them in this match and the momentum may carry over for them to get the win.

Prediction: The Brawling Birds take home the gold.

Jon Moxley in action in April 2025. (Lee South/AEW)

It has been a long and grueling Continental Challenge Cup and the finals will see continental champion Jon Moxley defend his title against Nigel McGuiness. Moxley is back on the All In card after losing the AEW World Championship to Adam Page last year. Moxley is looking for his own personal redemption and it may come at the expense of Nigel McGuiness, who is already battling an injury. McGuiness’ in-ring appearances have been few and far between but getting back in shape to make it through to the end is an accomplishment in and of itself. I don’t think Moxley can afford to lose this match.

Prediction: Moxley retains the AEW Continental Championship.

Chris Jericho appears during AEW Dynamite at Footprint Center in Phoenix, Ariz (Joe Camporeale/USA TODAY Sports)

The men’s Casino Gauntlet match will have a title shot waiting for the winner. The match has seen its own share of surprises in the past and this one may not be different. We already know who the initial entrants are: Andrade El Idolo, MJF, Tommaso Ciampa, Mark Davis and Chris Jericho. Nobody knows who else is going to be in this match, which could make for some wild in-ring action. MJF has the edge after winning this match last year at All In. Will he be able to pull it off again or is his focus too much on AEW national champion Andrade?

Prediction: It’s a wild one. Somehow, Chris Jericho sneaks away with the victory.

Mercedes Moné has been lusting to get back on top of the AEW women’s division since her return to the ring earlier this year. She won the Owen Hart Foundation Women’s Tournament to earn a shot at the AEW Women’s World Championship. After Willow Nightingale defeated Thekla at Redemption, the match at All In became more about the history between Moné and Nightingale than just the championship. Nightingale was the fourth-ever AEW TBS champion and held the belt for 35 days before Moné ended her first reign. Moné held that title for 584 days before Nightingale finally got her revenge. Nightingale was forced to give up her title due to an injury but made her way back to capture the AEW Women’s World Championship. Now, Moné is on her radar again and apparently delivered an on-screen hand injury to Nightingale on the final "Dynamite" before All In.

Prediction: Mercedes Moné picks up the title win.

Adam Copeland and Christian Cage win at AEW Double or Nothing in Queens, N.Y., on May 24, 2026. (Lee South/AEW)

The temps between the teams of Christian Cage and Adam Copeland and Matt and Nick Jackson have turned up ever since they teamed up at Grand Slam Mexico. Things between the teams got even more chaotic on "Dynamite" as Copeland was the last one standing when they butted heads. The AEW world tag titles have meant the world to have for Cope and Cage. But the Young Bucks have been a dominant force in tag team wrestling for years. It’s a fairly important matchup for the wrestling industry and it will be a treat to see these four men in the ring, going up against each other, at the same time.

Prediction: Cope and Cage retain in a great tag match.

Kenny Omega enters the ring during New Japan Pro-Wrestling's Wrestle Dynasty at Tokyo Dome on January 05, 2025 in Tokyo, Japan. (Etsuo Hara / Getty Images)

It’s the match everyone is waiting for: Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship. I don’t have to write too much on their history. Anyone who has ever watched pro wrestling knows the epic matches they put on in New Japan – some of the best matches in wrestling history. Both competitors are a little older now, and a little wiser. Omega is on top of the division as the champion after beating MJF at Spring Breakin’. Ospreay won the Owen Hart Foundation Men’s Tournament to earn the title shot, which everyone initially thought was going to be against MJF. But now Ospreay has a chance to dethrone his "hero" in Omega and do it in the main event at Wembley Stadium in his home country. Ospreay has been clear that it has always been his dream to be the focal point at Wembley and now he can be that and more.

Prediction: It is Will Ospreay’s time. Ospreay wins in a massive main event.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Trump confirms Pentagon plans for 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks, disputes report on Ground Zero absence
articles.excerpt:
After landing at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Aug. 28, 2026, President Donald Trump told reporters he'd be heading to the Pentagon for the 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks.

President Donald Trum...
articles.body_text:
After landing at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Aug. 28, 2026, President Donald Trump told reporters he'd be heading to the Pentagon for the 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks.

President Donald Trump said Friday that he's going to be at the Pentagon to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorists attacks.

A reporter on Friday asked the president why he was not planning to be in New York for the somber occasion.

"Because I'm going to the Pentagon," Trump shouted to the press at Joint Base Andrews.

On Thursday, The New York Times reported that Trump was not planning to attend the ceremony at Ground Zero, where the Twin Towers came down, because he wouldn't be allowed to give a speech. The annual event has banned politicians from speaking since 2012.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

President Donald Trump attends a ceremony at the Pentagon marking the 24th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks on Sept. 11, 2025. (Yasin Ozturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

When asked about the Times report, a White House spokeswoman called Trump a "proud New Yorker."

"President Trump has spoken about his own experiences watching the horrific events of September 11, 2001. On the 25th anniversary of this tragic day, the President will remember those who were killed at the hands of evil terrorists, honor their loved ones, and pay tribute to the brave first responders who put their lives on the line to rescue their fellow Americans," White House principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly said in a statement to Fox News.

"The vice president is still traveling to NYC and all three sites will be represented with administration officials in attendance," a White House official said, referring to the three Sept. 11 attack sites in Manhattan, at the Pentagon and near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, where United Airlines Flight 93 crashed.

After TMZ posted on X that Trump was "snubbing" the Ground Zero ceremony, White House communications director Steven Cheung fired back.

Donald Trump attends the annual 9/11 Commemoration Ceremony at the National 9/11 Memorial and Museum on Sept. 11, 2024, in New York City alongside then Vice President Kamala Harris, then-President Joe Biden, former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg and then-Sen. JD Vance, R-Ohio. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Trump lambasted the reporter behind in the Times article, writing on Truth Social Friday that she "made up a story that on September 11th, I’m not going to the World Trade Center, in New York City, because they won’t let me make a speech, and I’m going to the Pentagon in D.C., because I’m a featured speaker."

"This is more Corrupt News, I’ve been to New York many times over the years, and no one ever speaks, it’s a 'solemn ceremony!'" Trump wrote in part.

Trump said, "I would love not to speak, because I’m speaking all the time, and this is a day to remember the victims, and their beautiful family members."

Last year, Trump also chose to speak at the Pentagon for the 24th anniversary of 9/11, though he traveled to New York City later in the day to attend a Yankees game.

JUDGE THROWS OUT KHALID SHEIKH MOHAMMED'S 9/11 CONFESSION IN ALREADY LONG WAIT FOR TRIAL

The last time he attended the Ground Zero ceremony was in 2024, when he was the Republican presidential nominee. He was there alongside then-President Joe Biden and his election rival, then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

Trump also did not attend the Ground Zero ceremony during his first term. He spoke at the Pentagon in 2017, then alternated in subsequent years between commemorations there and at the site in Pennsylvania.

Donald Trump walks along the Wall of Names of the victims after a wreath-laying following a ceremony commemorating the 23rd anniversary of the crash of Flight 93 during the September 11th terrorist attacks at the Flight 93 National Memorial on Sept. 11, 2024, in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. (Jeff Swensen/Getty Images)

Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the terrorist attacks on Sept. 11, 2001, when al-Qaeda hijackers crashed three commercial airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. Hijackers also seized United Airlines Flight 93, but passengers fought back before the plane crashed in Pennsylvania.

The 9/11 attacks, which remain the deadliest in the nation's history, prompted the invasion of Afghanistan and helped usher in the broader War on Terror, which later included the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq.

Fox News' Patrick Ward contributed to this report.

James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

articles.title: Israeli settlers surround Palestinian home in occupied West Bank’s Qusra
articles.excerpt:
Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, have surrounded a Palestinian home in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank.

At least four Palestinians were trapped inside the h...
articles.body_text:
Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, have surrounded a Palestinian home in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank.

At least four Palestinians were trapped inside the home on Saturday while settlers set fire to nearby land, according to Al Jazeera journalists. Coordination is under way to allow ambulances to reach the area and evacuate one injured person.

Qusra has faced an escalating campaign of settler violence over the past month.

Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in the village in July, and since August 9 have besieged three Palestinian homes in the Ras al-Ain area, trapping families inside and cutting access to water, electricity and other essential supplies.

“We’re not allowed to live freely in and out of our houses; no one is allowed to bring us any food or visit us from family members or friends,” Loui Abu Raideh, one resident who has been trapped in his home for weeks, told Al Jazeera.

He said residents have to coordinate with the mayor of Qusra to get food and supplies, and it can take three to four days to get approval.

Israeli forces have declared the area a closed military zone and restricted Palestinians from entering and leaving, placing a gate at the main entrance of Qusra itself. Palestinians travelling into the village are forced to take alternative routes which are often blocked by Israeli forces.

On Wednesday, the Israeli military erected three new roadblocks at locations that encircled the top of the Ras al-Ain hill, disconnecting homes from the area below it.

Raideh said the feeling of being trapped is “a nightmare … 21 days, we can’t even sleep, we have to stay up at night [and] keep watching the security cameras, because those settlers can attack any time”.

Settler attacks – supported by the Israeli military – on Palestinian homes, businesses and farmland across the West Bank have been common for decades as illegal settlements have expanded across the territory.

The attacks have increased in intensity and frequency since Israel launched its genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza in October 2023, in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel.

articles.title: Exeter University approves deal with Saudi Arabia to train military officers and officials
articles.excerpt:
In move that could generate millions, Exeter academics to deliver MA at National Defense University in Riyadh

The University of Exeter has approved plans for a “formal partnership” with Saudi Arabia ...
articles.body_text:
In move that could generate millions, Exeter academics to deliver MA at National Defense University in Riyadh

The University of Exeter has approved plans for a “formal partnership” with Saudi Arabia to train senior military officers and government officials, despite long-held concerns about the Saudi government’s human rights record, the Guardian has learned.

In a deal that could generate millions of pounds for the Russell Group university, Exeter academics will deliver an MA in applied security and strategy (also known as an MStrat) to a cohort at the National Defense University (NDU) in Riyadh.

The MA will form the academic component of the NDU’s global strategy and strategic leadership programme, starting in 2026-27, and will be delivered to about 20 individuals per year, over three years. Until two years ago, the NDU was called the Saudi Armed Forces Command and Staff College.

The Saudi partnership has come to light at a time when the university is under fire from leading writers, broadcasters, academics and other alumni over plans to cut 150 jobs, primarily in the humanities, arts and social sciences, for which the highly ranked university is renowned.

The Exeter branch of the University and College Union (UCU) accused university managers of chasing “dirty money”.

A UCU spokesperson said: “We are horrified but hardly surprised to learn that management at Exeter are more interested in flogging military training to despotic regimes than in defending world-class humanities and social sciences teaching.”

The Exeter deal has not been widely publicised. It was approved by the university council in February this year, then endorsed by its senate the following month. In council minutes, seen by the Guardian, the partnership with the NDU is marked “Strictly confidential and commercial in confidence”.

In its marketing material, the university says the MStrat blends “academic depth with practical application”. It is aimed at working professionals in the armed forces, the government and international organisations and “offers a rigorous yet flexible environment in which to build strategic expertise”.

UK universities often sell consultancy and training to foreign governments via contracts worth millions of pounds. All such proposals have to be vetted first by university authorities to assess the legal, ethical and security risks of any potential collaboration.

Similar concerns were raised earlier this year when the Judge business school at the University of Cambridge put forward proposals to provide “leadership development” and “innovation management” to Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry. Senior academics described it as “horrifying” and a betrayal of the university’s commitments to freedom of expression.

Last month, the UK government announced the formation of a defence universities alliance – with Exeter among the 35 founding members – to “bring together academia and the armed forces” as part of a £182m investment to strengthen defence research and build critical skills.

A spokesperson for Exeter University said: “The MA in applied security and strategy has been taught at Exeter since 2012 through our strategy and security institute. Its students include serving British military personnel sponsored by the Ministry of Defence and Chevening scholars supported by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

“We are in discussions to deliver this established Exeter programme to a cohort at the National Defense University in Riyadh. Professional military education has formed part of the UK’s defence relationship with Saudi Arabia for many years, including through UK government institutions.

“Partnerships of this kind are assessed on academic and ethical grounds, through a process separate from budget planning.

“Like universities across the sector, Exeter continues to develop external partnerships and educational activity that supports our academic mission and enables our expertise to have impact in the UK and internationally.”

The UCU spokesperson responded: “Rather than chasing dirty money like this, we believe a university should be about protecting freedom of speech, upholding human rights and ensuring a wide range of brilliant courses and a fantastic student experience.”

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: number of missing climbs to nearly 3,000 as search for survivors enters fourth day – latest updates
articles.excerpt:
Nepali minister estimates cost of rebuilding could be up to $5bn, as death toll rises to 626 with seven confirmed dead in Tibet

‘The flood took everything I have’: survivors grieve for relatives and ...
articles.body_text:
Nepali minister estimates cost of rebuilding could be up to $5bn, as death toll rises to 626 with seven confirmed dead in Tibet

‘The flood took everything I have’: survivors grieve for relatives and homes swept away in Nepal

Chinese rescuers find ‘nothing but ruins’ at border crossing as Nepal seeks help to ID and store the dead

Thank you for joining us for our continuing coverage of the aftermath of Wednesday’s catastrophic flash floods in the Himalayan mountains near the Nepal-Tibet border.

Poor weather has hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal as the search for thousands of people missing enters its fourth day.

Nepal’s finance minister says his country will need up to $5bn to rebuild ⁠after the ⁠floods, believed to have been caused by a melting glacier high up in the mountains that set off a deadly cascade of water into the valleys below.

Finance ‌minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters ‌today those figures are “just an ​estimate” and that “loss and ⁠damage is ​being assessed”.

Nearly 3,000 people are missing. Nepal’s disaster agency on Saturday said 2,426 people were missing on its side of the border, while China’s Xinhua news agency reports the total number of missing in Tibet is now 554.

The death toll in Nepal has now risen to 626, while China’s Xinhua news agency earlier today reported seven people confirmed dead in Tibet.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far but at least 93,000 people are estimated to have been affected by the disaster, according to the Red Cross.

At least 777 foreigners are missing, with Nepal’s disaster agency on Friday reporting 517 foreigners unaccounted for – which could include tourists and foreign workers – and Chinese officials putting the number of foreigners missing at 260.

India said it is increasing surveillance of glaciers and glacial lakes in its Himalayan regions bordering Nepal and China.

The deadly floods on the Nepal-Tibet border were believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse that was detected as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event by geologists. You can read this explainer to find out more about how a collapsing glacier can generate a powerful flood, and whether the climate crisis is contributing to the risk.

Madan Kaushik, state disaster management minister in India’s Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, said: “Since we share a border with Nepal, as a neighbour, and also have a similar geographic situation … we have asked our department to monitor all the glaciers and known glacial lakes in the region.”

Uttarakhand is one of the most ecologically sensitive regions of India, with 1,266 glacial lakes. As glaciers melt, water can accumulate in lakes held back by natural barriers. If those barriers fail, vast volumes of water can be released suddenly, triggering devastating floods.

“We have asked our teams to be vigilant and monitor if a similar situation is emerging anywhere in the state,” Kaushik told AFP.

The Guardian’s south Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen and journalist Gaurav Pokharel report from the Nepalese town of Bidur, where rescue efforts are being coordinated. They spoke to survivors mourning loved ones and confronting the loss of their homes and livelihoods after devastating floods swept through their communities.

Among those caught in the floods was Sangke Dolma Tamang, who described the moment she watched her husband being swept away and returned to find her home and village destroyed:

double quotation markSangke Dolma Tamang, 61, had been cheerily cooking snacks in her village of Mailung in the Rasuwa district when the floods came without warning. The whole family ran uphill for safety, but as she grabbed for her husband, he slipped from her grip and was washed into the dark, fast-moving waters.

“Others tried to pull him to safety, but the flood swept him away,” she said, tears rolling down her weathered cheeks. There was, she said, nothing left of her village now. She had spent a night sheltering on higher ground, until an army helicopter arrived and brought to her safety at the barracks. Her son too was missing since the disaster, and she waited anxiously for any news.

“Now I have nothing left to live for,” said Tamang. “The whole house is gone. We couldn’t salvage anything.”

Nepal’s government has appealed for financial help as it faces the daunting task of recovering from the devastating flash floods and braces for the possibility of more flooding.

Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless or sheltering in temporary facilities.

“Multiple bridges have been washed away and major roads disrupted, leaving some of the worst-affected communities extremely difficult to reach,” the Red Cross says.

At least 18 schools have been destroyed and another 20 damaged, leaving about 10,000 school-age children affected, according to the UN Children’s Fund.

The disaster comes just ahead of the anniversary of last year’s 8-9 September mass anti-corruption protests that toppled the government.

Nepal is now led by prime minister Balendra Shah, a 36-year-old rapper turned politician widely known as “Balen”. The former Kathmandu mayor swept March elections on a wave of euphoria calling for political change.

The risk of a lake formed after the glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where the ⁠devastating flood occurred earlier ⁠this week has decreased, ​Chinese authorities said today, as its size appears to have shrunk.

Satellite images from Thursday this morning suggest water in the lake – straddling the China-Nepal border ⁠at the confluence of two rivers – has been slowly flowing through, decreasing the reservoir gradually, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the water resources ministry.

The ministry said satellite imagery of the surface area of the ⁠lake at Purepu Tsangpo river showed it was 99,000 sq metres in size this morning – around the size of ​14 football fields combined – having shrunk by 21,000 sq metres compared ‌with images from Thursday.

Experts and authorities have warned of the extremely high risk of secondary disasters in the valley, especially from the lake that was formed by glacier debris, potentially endangering rescue operations downstream.

State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, dispatched a 15-member team on Friday with reconnaissance drones, portable satellite stations and mobile surveillance cameras to gather more data about the ‌lake.

An overflow from the lake on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before further assessment deemed the risks manageable.

Thank you for joining us for our continuing coverage of the aftermath of Wednesday’s catastrophic flash floods in the Himalayan mountains near the Nepal-Tibet border.

Poor weather has hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal as the search for thousands of people missing enters its fourth day.
